title: [RFC] Cuda Graph Runner Backend Refactor
author: Oasis-Git
body:
## Background

Currently we have three cuda graph implementations: full cuda graph, torch-compile-based piecewise cuda graph (`TCPiecewiseCudaGraph`), and breakable cuda graph. There is a lot of duplicated code across the runners. We hope to refactor the whole code structure to unify them and make it clearer for users to understand the cuda graph code structure.

## Goal

Support flexible cuda graph backends across `(decode, prefill) x (full, breakable, torch-compile-based pcg)`. Enable breakable cuda graph for prefill by default.

## Proposed Design

### Part 1: Cuda Graph Implementation

**1. Runner**
- `PrefillCudaGraphRunner`: manages cuda graph execution for the prefill phase
- `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`: manages cuda graph execution for the decode phase

Both inherit from `BaseCudaGraphRunner`.

**2. Backend**
- `FullCudaGraphBackend`: captures the full model in a single cuda graph
- `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`: supports breaking out of the cuda graph for dynamic ops
- `TCPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`: torch-compile-based piecewise cuda graph

**Combination:** each runner owns a pluggable `BaseCudaGraphBackend`, giving a clean cross product of `(prefill, decode) x (full, breakable, tcpcg)`.

### Part 2: Arguments

Two types of arguments are supported:

**Config-based:** full control via a JSON config per phase, e.g.
`--cuda-graph-mode {"decode": "full", "prefill": "breakable"}`

**Convenience flags:** shorthand arguments that translate to the corresponding config, e.g.
- `--prefill-disable-cuda-graph` → `{"prefill": "disabled"}`
- `--decode-disable-cuda-graph` → `{"decode": "disabled"}`
- `--prefill-cuda-graph-bs` → sets batch sizes for prefill
- `--decode-cuda-graph-bs` → sets batch sizes for decode

## Impl
### Runner ↔ CudaGraphBackend Interaction (cg-refactor)

Two layers are in scope:

- **Phase runner** — `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` / `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`
  - Both subclass `BaseCudaGraphRunner`
  - Exactly one runner per phase
  - Fixed implementation

- **CG backend** — `BaseCudaGraphBackend` and its subclasses:
  - `FullCudaGraphBackend`
  - `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`
  - `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`
  - Pluggable per phase
  - Selected at initialization by:
    - `resolve_prefill_backend(model_runner)`
    - `resolve_decode_backend(model_runner)`
  - Backend type comes from:
    - `cuda_graph_config[phase].backend`

---

### Phase Runner API (`BaseCudaGraphRunner`)

Exposed upward to `ModelRunner`.

Each method delegates strategy-specific behavior to `self.backend`.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Determine whether the current batch can use a captured graph. Performs runner-level filtering before consulting the backend. |
| `capture()` | One-time capture entrypoint. Enumerates all capture shapes and invokes `capture_one_shape()` for each. |
| `capture_one_shape(size, ...)` | Captures a single shape. Builds a dummy forward batch and delegates actual capture to `self.backend.capture_one(...)`. |
| `replay_prepare(forward_batch, **kwargs) -> ForwardBatch` | Pads or reshapes inputs to match a captured shape and returns the static batch used during replay. |
| `replay(forward_batch, ...) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the captured graph via `self.backend.replay(...)`. |

---

### CG Backend API (`BaseCudaGraphBackend`)

Exposed downward to the phase runner.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `prepare(runner)` | One-time setup against the owning runner. Wires static buffers, patches the model module, and installs forward hooks. |
| `setup_prefill_state(runner)` *(prefill only)* | Additional one-time initialization for prefill-specific state. |
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Strategy-specific runtime gate. Examples: BCG rejects sparse-DP batches; TcPiecewise checks `torch.compile` state. |
| `capture_session(stream)` *(context manager)* | Wraps the entire capture phase. Sets graph-pool ID, capture flags, allocator hints, etc. |
| `capture_one(num_tokens, ...)` | Captures a single shape. The runner provides the dummy batch; the backend performs warmup and recorded forward execution. |
| `has_shape(shape_key) -> bool` | Returns whether a recorded graph exists for the given shape. Used by `runner.can_run()`. |
| `runtime_session()` *(context manager)* | Wraps a replay execution. Sets replay flags, locks caches, and scopes graph resources. |
| `replay(shape_key, forward_batch) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the recorded graph corresponding to the shape key. |
| `populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)` *(prefill only)* | Fills capture-time placeholders so recorded graphs observe stable input addresses. |
| `commit_prefill_serving_inputs(forward_batch)` *(prefill only)* | Copies real serving inputs into static buffers immediately before replay. |
| `cleanup()` | Releases graph pools and removes any model patching. |

---

### Runner → Backend Interaction

#### Initialization

Once per runner:

    runner.init
    └─ self.backend = resolve_{prefill,decode}_backend(model_runner)
       ├─ self.backend.prepare(self)
       └─ prefill only:
          └─ self.backend.setup_prefill_state(self)

---

#### Capture

Once, across all capture shapes:

    runner.capture()
    └─ with backend.capture_session(stream):
       └─ for size in capture_shapes:
          └─ runner.capture_one_shape(size)
             ├─ build dummy forward_batch
             │  └─ runner-owned logic
             ├─ prefill only:
             │  └─ backend.populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)
             └─ backend.capture_one(num_tokens, ...)
                └─ warmup + recorded forward

---

#### Replay

Per forward, on the hot path:

    ModelRunner.forward(batch)
    ├─ if not runner.can_run(batch):
    │  └─ fall back to eager
    │
    │     runner.can_run() internally consults:
    │     - backend.has_shape(...)
    │     - backend.can_run(...)
    │
    ├─ static_batch = runner.replay_prepare(batch)
    │  └─ prefill only:
    │     └─ backend.commit_prefill_serving_inputs(batch)
    │
    └─ with backend.runtime_session():
       └─ output = backend.replay(shape_key, static_batch)

---

### Backend-Specific Overrides

| Backend | Capture mechanism | Distinct overrides |
|---|---|---|
| `FullCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` over the entire model forward | `capture_session()`, `capture_one()`, `replay()` |
| `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` | Multiple `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` segments stitched at `eager_on_graph` breakpoints | `capture_one()`, `replay()`, plus per-segment metadata in `attn_metadata_buffers` |
| `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` with FX-level piecewise splits | `prepare()` installs compile hooks; `capture_one()` drives `torch.compile` warmup; no direct graph replay recording because `torch.compile` owns execution |

---

### Where the Seam Matters

The runner/backend boundary is the extensibility point.

Adding a new CUDA Graph strategy requires:

1. Creating a new `BaseCudaGraphBackend` subclass.
2. Registering it in the backend factory.

The phase runner code should remain unchanged.

This refactor replaces the previous design where each strategy required its own runner implementation.

The strict API contract is the runner call points listed above. If a new strategy requires additional coordination, the corresponding hook should be added to `BaseCudaGraphBackend` so that all runners can drive the strategy uniformly.

## Plan

1. Breakable cuda graph #22218
2. Cuda graph runner/backend refactor #23906 
3. Default mode (`{"decode": "full", "prefill": "breakable"}`) enable #29458

title: RFC: optional HIP external LLMM1 fast path for M=1 decode GEMMs
author: skyguan92
body:
# Summary

I validated a narrow HIP decode fast path on `gfx1151` ROCm and would like maintainer feedback before proposing it as a merge-ready change.

The idea is:

- keep the existing path as default
- add an optional HIP-only fast path inside `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply()`
- lazily load an external op
- route only eligible `M=1` skinny-GEMM decode shapes into that op
- cleanly fall back if the op is unavailable

The specific external op used in my experiments was:

- `torch.ops._rocm_C.LLMM1`

## Why I think this is worth discussing

On this setup, the remaining decode gap was not in the attention kernel path. After profiling and A/B experiments, the dominant remaining gap for `p1/g64` was the small-batch dense GEMM path.

Service-level results:

- upstream-clean baseline (`32768 + bf16 KV`):
  - `p220/g1 repeat = 1059.31 tok/s`
  - `p1/g64 repeat = 13.3591 tok/s`
- same serving class with the optional HIP `LLMM1` route:
  - `p220/g1 repeat = 1061.07 tok/s`
  - `p1/g64 repeat = 20.9811 tok/s`

So:

- prefill: essentially unchanged
- decode: about `+57%`

The same route was also validated on a larger-capacity profile (`131072 + fp8 KV`) and still held decode around `20.36 tok/s`.

## Narrow activation conditions

The fast path only activates when all of the following are true:

- HIP
- env enabled
- external `.so` path provided
- `bias is None`
- input dtype is `fp16` or `bf16`
- input device is HIP/CUDA
- `n == 1`
- `m % 4 == 0`
- `k <= 8192`

Otherwise it falls back to the existing implementation.

## Main question for maintainers

Would SGLang accept an **optional external HIP op hook** for a narrow decode fast path like this?

More specifically, is the dependency boundary below acceptable in principle:

- lazy-load an external shared object
- bind an optional op such as `torch.ops._rocm_C.LLMM1`
- keep the feature disabled by default
- fall back cleanly when unavailable

If the answer is no, that is still useful feedback. In that case I would treat this as evidence for the performance opportunity, but not propose the external-op integration directly.

## If maintainers are open to it

I already prepared:

- a narrow patch draft against `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py`
- a PR draft with suggested tests and env contract

I can open the PR immediately after getting a signal that this integration boundary is acceptable enough to review.

title: [RFC] GLM-5 Spec. Decode + PP in Disaggregation Decode Mode
author: MMuzzammil1
body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation I'd briefly share my plan of action on how we can support Speculative Decoding + PP in Disagg Decode Mode. Feel free to drop your comments/suggestions. ## Model Weights Layout - The speculative model weights will be duplicated loaded on `first_pp_rank` and `last_pp_rank`: - This implies duplicate `lm_head` on the `first_pp_rank` and duplicate `embed` on the `last_pp_rank`. - The target model weights will be set-up in the regular PP setting. ## Flow - Draft Phase would happen on the `first_pp_rank` -> `draft_tokens`, `scores` would be sent to each PP-rank via the `PPProxyTensors` already implemented. - Each individual PP-rank would materialize `build_tree_kernel_efficient()` to get `EagleVerifyInput`. - The last PP-rank would run the `verify()` to get the `accepted_tokens` -> `verify_metadata` sent to the `first_pp_rank`. - The last PP-rank would also run `forward_draft_extend_after_decode()`. - `_prep_batch_result` would run the `post_process_after_verify(verify_metadata)` to update request states (finished/unfinished) and free unused KV-slots on the first PP-rank. - `verify_metadata` would then be passed along to PP-1..PP-2 and so on for request state adjustment on each PP-rank. ## Diagram ## Speculative Decoding + Pipeline Parallelism in Disagg Decode Mode (Flow of a Microbatch) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant C as Client participant PP0 as first_pp_rank
(PP0) participant PPn as middle_pp_ranks
(PP-1..PP-N-2) participant PPL as last_pp_rank
(PP-N-1) note over PP0: Hosts: embed + mtp_layer + lm_head
+ target model (first PP shard) note over PPL: Hosts: embed + mtp_layer + lm_head
+ target model (last PP shard) note over PPn: Hosts: target model (middle PP shard) C->>PP0: Decode Request note over PP0: Draft Phase PP0->>PP0: set_kv_cache(kv_buffer, index_k_with_scale_buffer)
received from last PP-N-1 PP0->>PP0: draft() → EagleDraftOutput
(also includes the kv_buffer, index_k_with_scale_buffer values for new tokens populated) note over PP0: Tree Building PP0->>PP0: build_tree_kernel_efficient() → EagleVerifyInput note over PP0: Target Forward PP0->>PP0: forward() -> hidden_states PP0->>PPn: PPProxyTensors(hidden_states, EagleDraftOutput) note over PPn: Tree Building PPn->>PPn: build_tree_kernel_efficient() → EagleVerifyInput note over PPn: Target Forward PPn->>PPn: forward() -> hidden_states PPn->>PPL: PPProxyTensors(hidden_states, EagleDraftOutput) note over PPL: Tree Building PPL->>PPL: build_tree_kernel_efficient() → EagleVerifyInput note over PPL: Target Forward + Verify PPL->>PPL: foward() → hidden_states, logits PPL->>PPL: verify() -> verify_metadata[accepted_tokens, pages_to_free,...] note over PPL: Draft Extend PPL->>PPL: set_kv_cache(kv_buffer, index_k_with_scale_buffer) PPL->>PPL: forward_draft_extend_after_decode() -> EagleDraftOutput
(kv_buffer, index_k_with_scale_buffer values,...) PPL-->>PP0: PPProxyTensors(verify_metadata, EagleDraftOutput, ...) note over PP0: Post-Process PP0->>PP0: _prep_batch_result()
post_process_after_verify(verify_metadata)
→ update request states, free KV-slots ``` ## Target Worker - I plan to extend `EagleWorker` module for this support (since PP doesn't support overlap mode anyways so there's no point working with `EagleWorker2`. ## Concerns - On why mtp layer needs to be loaded on both first and last PP ranks: - For the target model to verify, we need drafted token outputs before the target forward run -> need to obtain the draft tokens on the first PP rank itself. - `batch` can get modified when we get the `get_next_disagg_decode_batch_to_run()` on first PP rank. Both `draft()` and `draft_extend_after_decode()` need to run on the same `batch`, one before target model forward, other afterwards. - Since `draft()` happens on first PP-rank and the `draft_extend_after_decode()` happens on last PP-rank, there is a necessity to pass `incremental KV values` across PP-ranks -> Need some feedback on the feasibility of doing this. - Performance: Would an implementation like this be performant or not. Need some feedback on this as well. ### Related resources Relevant Files: - `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker.py` - `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_pp_mixin.py` - `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py`, `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py` (`GLMMoeDsaForCausalLM`'s base class)

title: [RFC] Sglang non-GPU process rust migration
author: rainj-me
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

**PR**
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29799

Refer Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22949
Release Roadmap https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0

### Motivation

**Status**: Draft
**Author**: @rainj-me
**Created**: Apr 20 2026
**Version**: 0.1

# Rust Server Migration Plan

**Status:** Draft · **Last updated:** 2026-06-18 · **Owner:** Rain Jiang

Migration of the SGLang request front-half (everything from network ingress up to
the point a tokenized request is handed to the GPU scheduler) from Python to a
multi-threaded Rust implementation.

---

## 1. Goals & scope

**Goal.** Replace the Python tokenizer/detokenizer managers and HTTP server with a
single-process, thread-per-core Rust implementation that owns the request lifecycle
up to scheduler submission.

**In scope:** HTTP(S)/gRPC/WS/h2/h3 server, request FSM, tokenizer & detokenizer
managers, multimodal encoder dispatch, control API (abort/flush/weight update etc.),
large tensor zero-copy handoff to the scheduler, cross-dp-group dispatch.

**Out of scope (this plan):** model kernels, attention backends, KV-cache internals,
quantization. The Rust server keeps the existing Python scheduler and GPU worker framework; it does not reimplement them.

**Non-goals:** behavioral changes to the public API. The Rust server must be a
drop-in for the Python one — same endpoints, same request/response schemas, same
streaming semantics — so it can ship behind a flag and be A/B'd against Python.

---

## 2. Architecture summary

The design this phase implement (decided separately; recorded here for context):

- **Two FSMs, one process.** An **ingress FSM** (per request, multi-threaded,
  thread-per-core) carrying a request from `Received` through validation and
  optional encode/tokenize to `Queued`; and an **egress FSM** handling streaming
  (`Streaming` self-loop → `Finalizing` → `Completed`). They are the two halves of
  one request's lifecycle, owned by the same core and meeting at the ring-buffer /
  scheduler boundary — no shared locks.
- **Six thread groups:** (1) **api-server** on an async runtime — accepts
  connections, terminates protocols; (2) **tokenizer-manager** running the
  ingress/egress request FSMs, CPU-core-bound; (3) **encoder** (core-bound);
  (4) **tokenizer** (core-bound); (5) **detokenizer** (core-bound); and
  (6) the python **scheduler** group within main thread. Groups talk only via channels — no shared locks across group boundaries.
- **Channels:** bounded **MPSC** TokenizerManager→Scheduler (`try_send` = backpressure), per-core **SPSC** returns; userspace rings carry the payload, no ZMQ involved. Crossing the Rust→Python boundary, request objects are serialized with **msgpack** so only immutable bytes transfer — keeping the GIL out of the hot path. Tensor data bypasses msgpack entirely and is shared through **pinned memory**, handed across as a handle rather than copied or serialized.
- **Zero-copy:** for encoded multimodal data, Python pre-allocates the pinned buffer pool at startup and Rust writes into slots by index during the encode/tokenize phase. Channels move slot handles (plus small msgpack metadata), never tensor bytes; lifetime is the pool's slot-reuse policy — a slot returns to the free list only after both Python's read and any GPU DMA complete, not Rust's `Drop`.
- **Cross-rank:** For DP attention, the first rank of each DP group runs the Rust server
  *without* the api-server; a single api-server then fans **control** messages to
  every DP group (duplicated, since control must reach all), while **generation**
  requests are **round-robined** across DP groups for load balancing.
- **Streaming:** a single `Streaming` macro state self-loops per chunk; non-streaming
  is just a stream whose frames are accumulated and emitted in `Finalizing`.

See the request-FSM and topology diagrams in the Appendix for detail.

---

## 3. Phase 1 — Rust server (tok/detok manager + HTTP server)

**Target: 2026-07-17**

Phase 1 delivers the Rust front-half running in front of the **existing Python
scheduler + GPU worker**, inside one process via multi-threaded Rust ⇄ Python.

### 3.1 Work breakdown

|  | Item | Status | Depends on | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Rust frontend \+ scheduler PoC | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#23360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23360) \[Closed\] |
| 2 | Architecture design | ✅ Done | — | Pending final approval |
| 3 | Pickle → msgpack migration | ✅ Done | — | PR [\#28688](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28688) \[Merged\] Followup issue [\#29465](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29465)  |
| 4 | Single-process framework: multi-threaded Rust \+ Python scheduler/GPU worker | ✅ Done | 3 |  |
| 5 | Tokenizer & detokenizer manager | ✅ Done | 4 |  |
| 6 | HTTP server: /generate \+ streaming | ✅ Done | 4, 5 |  |
| 7 | Encoder support | 🟡 WIP | 4, 5 | Work with dynamo team check whether this can export to dynamo crate. |
| 8 | PD disaggregation | ✅Done | 4 | Large. Prefill/decode split — see risk note. |
| 9 | DP attention \+ cross-node DP controller | ✅ Done | 4 | Large, cross-node. See risk note. |
| 10 | Metrics / logging | 🟡 WIP | 4 | Logging Done, Metrics WIP |
| 11 | Port existing HTTP APIs other than the listed APIs below | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Full endpoint parity for drop-in replacement. |
| 12 | Unified multi-protocol lib (server \+ gateway) | ⏳ Pending | 6 | Shared http(s)/h2/h3/gRPC/WS layer reused by sglang-gateway. |
| 13 | Code Refactor | 🟡 WIP |  |  |
| 14 | AuthZ support |  |  |  |
| 15 | Parallel Sampling |  |  |  |
| 16 | Benchmark\_serving perf optimization | 🟡 WIP |  |  |
| 17 | Embedding request |  |  |  |
| 18  | offline Engine API support |  |  |  |
| 19 | Other flags in the TokenizedGenerateReqInput  |  |  |  |
| 20 | cache\_tokens |  |  |  |
| 21 | custom\_logit\_processor |  |  |  |
| 22 | preferred\_sampling\_params |  |  |  |
| 23 | Standalone API-Server for DP Attn | 🟡 WIP |  |  |
| 24 | Anthorpic API support |  |  |  |
| 25 | SageMaker API support |  |  |  |
| 26 | Vertex AI API support |  |  |  |
| 27 | Ollama compatible API support |  |  |  |
| 28 | Weight update APIs |  |  |  |
| 29 | HiCache APIs |  |  |  |

### 3.2 Sequencing & critical path

Items are **not** independent. The dependency spine is:

```
#3 pickle→msgpack  ──►  #4 single-process framework  ──►  #5 tok/detok  ──►  #6 /generate+stream  ──►  #11 API parity
                                              └─►  #10 metrics (parallel)
                                              └─►  #7 encoder (parallel, after #5)
```

**Critical path to a usable July 17 milestone:** 3 → 4 → 5 → 6, with 10 landing in
parallel and 11 close behind. That subset is what makes the Rust server a working,
A/B-testable drop-in for text LLM traffic.

**Recommend deferring out of the July 17 milestone** (track as Phase 1.5 / stretch):
items **8 (PD disaggregation)** and **9 (DP attention + cross-node DP controller)**.
Both are large, both can land after the core path is proven, and bundling them into
the July date puts the whole milestone at risk. Item **12 (unified protocol lib)** is
valuable but is a refactor that can follow once #6 stabilizes the protocol surface.

> **Date reality check.** July 17 is ~4 weeks out and #4 (the foundation) is still
> pending-start. The 3→4→5→6+7 path is achievable in that window if #4 starts
> immediately and 8/9/12 are explicitly descoped. Carrying all 12 to July 17 is not
> realistic; pick the milestone definition deliberately.

### 3.3 Phase 1 exit criteria

- Rust server handles `/generate` (streaming + non-streaming) at parity with Python.
- Tok/detok managers run in-process; detok is incremental and order-correct.
- Encoder path works for at least one multimodal input type.
- Metrics + logs at parity; runs behind a flag, A/B-able against Python.
- Endpoint parity sufficient to route production text traffic.

---

## 4. Cross-cutting concerns

**Rollout / fallback.** Every phase ships behind a flag with the Python path as the
live fallback. Migrate by traffic slice (shadow → small % → ramp), not big-bang. keep the Python path runnable as the live fallback until the Rust path reaches parity.

**Testing.** Differential testing against Python (same inputs → same tokens/frames)
is the primary correctness gate. Add: FSM property tests (every state has a terminal
exit; post-terminal events are no-ops/idempotent); streaming order + UTF-8-boundary
tests for detok.

**Observability.** Metrics/logging (P1 #10) should land *with* the core path, not
after — debugging the channel/FSM/threading layers without it is painful. Per-state
request counts, queue depths (ring-buffer occupancy = backpressure signal), per-core
load, and control-op latencies.

**Kernel / environment.** io_uring features used (`MSG_RING` 5.18+, `SEND_ZC` 6.0+,
`DEFER_TASKRUN` 6.1+) set a minimum kernel; some hardened/container environments
disable io_uring — keep an epoll+eventfd fallback behind the same loop abstraction.

---

## 5. Top risks

| Risk                                              | Impact                            | Mitigation                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| July 17 scope (all 12 items)                      | Milestone slips / quality suffers | Descope 8/9/12; define milestone as 3→4→5→6+10.                              |
| #4 framework is the foundation and hasn't started | Blocks 5–7; whole phase waits     | Start immediately; treat as the single highest-priority item.                |
| Rust↔Python boundary in the single-process step   | Perf cliffs, GIL contention       | Keep the boundary narrow (handles, not data); measure early.                 |
| Detok ordering / UTF-8 under streaming            | Corrupt user-visible output       | Shard by `hash(req_id)`; stateful decode offsets; boundary tests.            |
| Slow-client backpressure on egress                | GPU stalls / memory growth        | Bounded egress buffers; treat persistent slow consumer as disconnect.        |

---

## 6. Milestones

| Date       | Milestone                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ~Now       | #1 PR #23360, #3 merged (PR #28688); #4 started.                                                                        |
| 2026-07-17 | **Phase 1 core:** Rust server with `/generate` + streaming + encoder + metrics, A/B-able vs Python (items 3–7, 10, 11). |
| Phase 1.5  | PD disaggregation (#8), DP attention + cross-node controller (#9), unified protocol lib (#12).                          |


## 7. Appendix

1. [Initial plan](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Y71GY3DOzZwuAp2ytehW0rJ4uzOx276PMtgTORgD49c/edit?slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0#slide=id.g3e59bc0132c_0_0)
2. [Architecture Design](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1_DJ_Fjq_tgMTmzWcmm5uacCi9RJGW_lwZGeXiecc6XY/edit?slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0#slide=id.g3eebae54d8d_0_0)

title: [Feature][RFC] Plug-in metrics backend via class-level DI for collectors
author: nadongjun
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation


When SGLang runs as an embedded engine inside downstream serving infrastructure (Ray Serve LLM, custom inference platforms), the metric storage backend is locked to `prometheus_client` at import time. The five `*MetricsCollector` classes in `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py` instantiate `Counter`, `Gauge`, `Histogram`, and `Summary` directly. Embedded users have three workarounds today:

| Workaround | Cost |
|---|---|
| Tail `--export-metrics-to-file` output | Operational complexity; filesystem path coupling; file rotation handling |
| Scrape `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` directly | Couples downstream code to internal metric names and label keys |

`RequestMetricsExporter` ([#11141](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/11141) / [#10973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10973)) opened the request-finish event layer to plug-ins. The storage layer behind every collector remains hardcoded. To close that gap and follow the pattern proven in vLLM (`vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py` plus the `_gauge_cls` / `_counter_cls` / `_histogram_cls` indirection on `PrometheusStatLogger`), we propose two PRs:

**1. Class-level DI on collectors and `stat_loggers` Engine kwarg [[PR]](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24610):** Refactor the five `*MetricsCollector` classes to instantiate metrics through `_gauge_cls`, `_counter_cls`, `_histogram_cls`, and `_summary_cls` class attributes. Defaults stay at the current `prometheus_client` classes, so existing deployments see no change. Add an optional `Dict[str, type]` field `stat_loggers` on `ServerArgs`. Keys are collector roles; values are subclasses of the matching base collector. The five instantiation sites read from this map and fall back to the base class. Class-object kwarg only; CLI exposure is omitted because import-path string parsing is fragile and unnecessary for embedded use cases. The DI refactor and the kwarg ship together because the refactor alone has no public consumer.

   Affected collectors:

   | Collector | Metric count | Uses `Summary`? |
   |---|---|---|
   | `SchedulerMetricsCollector` | 77 | Yes (one feature-flagged metric, `eplb_balancedness`, gated on `SGLANG_ENABLE_EPLB_BALANCEDNESS_METRIC`) |
   | `TokenizerMetricsCollector` | 12 | No |
   | `StorageMetricsCollector` | 6 | No |
   | `RadixCacheMetricsCollector` | 4 | No |
   | `ExpertDispatchCollector` | 1 | No |

   `_summary_cls` is added on `SchedulerMetricsCollector` only.

**2. Reference Ray wrappers [PR]:** Add `python/sglang/srt/observability/ray_wrappers.py` mirroring vLLM's wrapper file. Provides `RayGaugeWrapper`, `RayCounterWrapper`, `RayHistogramWrapper`, `RaySummaryWrapper` on top of `ray.util.metrics`, plus five `Ray*MetricsCollector` subclasses overriding the class attrs from PR 1. The base class handles Ray Serve replica context (`_get_replica_id()`) and OTel-compliant name sanitization. `ray.util.metrics` rejects `:` in names, so `sglang:foo` becomes `sglang_foo`. Imported only when the caller routes metrics to Ray.

### Usage

Embedded users swap the metric storage backend in one place. Example for Ray Serve LLM:

```python
import sglang
from sglang.srt.observability.ray_wrappers import (
    RaySchedulerMetricsCollector,
    RayTokenizerMetricsCollector,
    RayStorageMetricsCollector,
    RayRadixCacheMetricsCollector,
    RayExpertDispatchCollector,
)

engine = sglang.Engine(
    model_path="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    enable_metrics=True,
    stat_loggers={
        "scheduler": RaySchedulerMetricsCollector,
        "tokenizer": RayTokenizerMetricsCollector,
        "storage": RayStorageMetricsCollector,
        "radix_cache": RayRadixCacheMetricsCollector,
        "expert_dispatch": RayExpertDispatchCollector,
    },
)
```

All ~100 `sglang:*` metrics now flow directly to `ray.util.metrics`, with Ray Serve labels (`application` / `deployment` / `replica`) appended automatically. The samples appear on Ray's Prometheus endpoint:

```bash
$ curl -s http://ray-cluster:8080/metrics | grep ray_serve_sglang_ | head
ray_serve_sglang_prompt_tokens_total{model_name="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",tp_rank="0",replica="...",...} 8128902
ray_serve_sglang_num_running_reqs{...} 8
ray_serve_sglang_token_usage{...} 0.28
ray_serve_sglang_time_to_first_token_seconds_bucket{le="0.1",...} 254
```

The same hook can target OpenTelemetry, Datadog, or in-house telemetry by supplying a different set of subclasses. SGLang itself does not integrate with any specific vendor.

For users not setting `stat_loggers`, behavior is unchanged. Existing CLI flags, `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR`, and Grafana dashboards keep working without modification.

### Backward compatibility

| Concern | Status |
|---|---|
| Existing `prometheus_client`-based deployments | No change. Defaults preserved |
| Existing metric names (`sglang:foo`) | No change. Only Ray wrapper sanitizes names |
| Existing Grafana dashboards | No change |
| Existing `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` env behavior | No change |
| Existing CLI flags (`--enable-metrics`, `--export-metrics-to-file`, ...) | No change |
| Anyone not setting `stat_loggers` | Gets today's behavior |

### Related resources

| Reference | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [vllm-project/vllm `vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/metrics/ray_wrappers.py) | Working implementation of the proposed pattern |
| [vllm-project/vllm `vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py) | `PrometheusStatLogger` showing the class-attr pattern |
| [ray-project/ray#62791](https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/62791) | Downstream tracking issue (use case driving this RFC) |

title: [RFC] [HiCache] A new backend for external L3 storage systems
author: stepinto
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## 1. Summary

This RFC proposes a vendor-neutral RPC connector for HiCache. A standalone StorageServer process sits beside SGLang; KV tensor data is accessed directly through a shared `memfd` region (zero-copy), while gRPC over a UNIX domain socket carries only keys and iovec descriptors.

A prototype backend is developed to demonstrate this idea.

---

## 2. Motivation

HiCache already ships several storage backend integrations:

| Backend | Constraint |
|---------|-----------|
| `mooncake_store` | Requires the Mooncake distributed caching system |
| `hf3fs` | Requires the HF3FS distributed filesystem |
| `nixl` | Bound to NVIDIA hardware and ecosystem |
| `aibrix_kvcache` | Bound to the Alibrix cloud platform |
| `eic` | Bound to Volcengine cloud platform |

Each integration lives in-tree and introduces a compile-/import- time dependency on a third-party system. As a result:

- Vendors who want to connect their own storage system must submit and maintain code inside the SGLang repository.
- New storage systems cannot be plugged in without touching SGLang internals.

The FUSE filesystem in Linux solves the analogous problem for filesystems: it defines a clear and stable wire interface so that any filesystem can be implemented in user space without changing the kernel. We want the same property for HiCache storage.

A vendor-neutral connector also benefits the SGLang community directly:

- Infrastructure teams can connect proprietary or cloud-vendor-specific storage without upstreaming confidential code.
- Research teams can prototype new caching strategies without forking SGLang.
- The SGLang core remains clean: one small, well-defined interface instead of an ever-growing list of vendor integrations.

---

## 3. Goals

- **Vendor neutrality**.  The protocol must not reference, favor, or require any particular cache system, hardware vendor, or cloud provider. SGLang treats every conforming storage server equally.
- **Stable protocol**.  Provide a stable wire-format, so that an out-of-tree L3 storage system may work across multiple versions of SGLang.
- **Minimal overhead**.  Keep the hot-path (data transfer) overhead small: KV tensors reside in a shared memory region visible to both SGLang and the storage server, so the data path requires no copy — only addresses and lengths are transmitted via UDS.
- **Language agnostic**.  Storage servers can be written in Python, Rust, C++, etc.
- **Handle StorageServer restarts smoothly**.  The main portion of L3 storage code lives in a standalone process called StorageServer, which could be upgraded or restarted without restarting SGLang.  During that period of StorageServer restart, SGLang works as if L3 cache is empty, and more importantly no loss of L2 memory cache.
 
---

## 4. Non-Goals

- Replace existing in-tree backends. Those backends remain as first-class citizens for users who prefer them.
- Mandate any particular storage algorithm or eviction policy on the L3 server side; the protocol is deliberately opaque to storage internals.

---

## 5. Design

We will firstly present an overview, and then dive into issues in detail.

### 5.1. Architecture Overview

```
  ┌──────────────────┐                  ┌──────────────────┐
  │ SGLang tp_rank=0 │ ── uds & shm ──▶ │                  │
  ├──────────────────┤                  │  Standalone L3   │
  │ SGLang tp_rank=1 │ ── uds & shm ──▶ │                  |
  ├──────────────────┤                  │  Storage Server  │
  │       ...        │ ── uds & shm ──▶ │                  │
  └──────────────────┘                  └──────────────────┘
```

Two sockets are used:

- `mempool_socket` — a raw UNIX domain socket used exclusively for the `RegisterPool` handshake (shared memory FD exchange).
- `grpc_socket` — a UNIX domain socket carrying the gRPC StorageServer service (metadata, iovec descriptors).

Separating them keeps FD passing (which requires `SCM_RIGHTS` and a custom framing) completely out of the gRPC layer.

### 5.2 Shared Memory: RegisterPool

Before any data transfer can occur, each SGLang TP rank registers its host KV cache pool with the storage server. Registration transfers the memory region to the server without copying:

```
  sglang                           storage
    │         RegisterPool          │
    │──────────────────────────────▶│
    │           pool_id             │
    │◀──────────────────────────────│
    │                               │
    │     (connection stays open)   │
```

Wire format on `mempool_socket`:

1. 8-byte little-endian magic (`0x8DF6FBFD`), chosen to be distinct from the HTTP/2 client preface.
2. `uint32` little-endian name length, followed by the pool name bytes.
3. Ancillary data: exactly one file descriptor via `SCM_RIGHTS` (a `memfd` holding the KV tensor buffer).

On success the server replies with a 4-byte little-endian `pool_id` (allocated monotonically from 1). The connection must remain open for the lifetime of the registration; closing it signals the server to unmap the region.

This mechanism avoids any copy through the kernel on the data path: both SGLang and the storage server have a direct `mmap` view of the same physical pages.

### 5.3 RPC Protocol

```protobuf
service StorageServer {
  // Handshake adn exchange capabilities between sglang and storage server.
  rpc Capabilities(CapabilitiesRequest) returns (CapabilitiesResponse)

  // Test if keys exist.
  rpc BatchExist(BatchExistRequest) returns (BatchExistResponse);

  // Store.
  rpc BatchPut(BatchPutRequest) returns (BatchPutResponse);

  // Retrieve.
  rpc BatchGet(BatchGetRequest) returns (BatchGetResponse);
}

// Reference to a continious portion of data in the memory pool specified by `pool_id`.
message Iovec {
  fixed64 ptr = 1;
  fixed32 length = 2;
}

// A single PUT or GET request.
message Transfer {
  bytes id = 1;
  repeated Iovec iovec = 2;
  int32 pool_id = 3;
}

message BatchGetRequest {
  repeated Transfer gets = 1;
}

...
```

All tensor data travels via the shared memory pool identified by `pool_id`. gRPC messages carry only keys, iovec descriptors, and result codes — never raw tensor bytes. This keeps gRPC message sizes small and eliminates the serialisation cost for bulk data.

### 5.4 gRPC or other?

Three alternatives were considered:

- **Custom binary protocol over UDS**. Serialisation overhead is lower, but maintaining a stable interface across versions requires hand-rolled framing and versioning logic. Any breaking change would require coordinated updates on both the SGLang side and every out-of-tree storage server. The maintenance burden outweighs the performance benefit, especially given that gRPC messages on this path carry only keys and small iovec descriptors — not bulk tensor data.

- **Other RPC systems**.  It would be nice to have a RPC system FD passing and memory sharing. To our knowledge, there are no popular RPC systems that support this. 

- **NVMe-style submission/completion queues with an eventfd doorbell**. This pattern can achieve very low per-operation latency, but it introduces significant implementation complexity: shared ring-buffer management, memory ordering, and a bespoke flow-control protocol. The connector's goal is to be easy to implement from scratch in any language; a lock-free queue protocol raises the barrier too high.

- **Multiplex registration and gRPC on a single port**. In principle the two protocols could share one socket: we may distinguish two kinds of connections by peeking the a few bytes.  In practice, the Python gRPC server does not support it.

Therefore, we choose gRPC over UDS. In fact, gRPC is already an indirect dependency of SGLang (introduced by smg-grpc-servicer and opentelemetry-exporter-otlp), so there is no extra dependency to install. The protobuf schema makes it easy to maintain compatibility.

### 5.5 Failure Handling

#### 5.5.1 SGLang crash / restart

The registration connection on `mempool_socket` stays open for the pool's lifetime. When SGLang crashes, the OS closes the FD and the storage server detects the UDS disconnect, treating it as an implicit deregistration: it unmaps the `memfd` region and releases the `pool_id`. On restart, SGLang re-runs the `RegisterPool` handshake and receives a new `pool_id`; previously persisted cache entries remain accessible by key.

#### 5.5.2 StorageServer crash / restart

When the storage server becomes unavailable, SGLang detects the `mempool_socket` disconnect and gRPC errors, then enters degraded mode: `BatchPut` returns success immediately, `Exist` and `BatchGet` always reports a miss. SGLang continues serving inference requests as if L3 is empty. In the background, it retries the `RegisterPool` handshake at a configurable interval; a successful reply exits degraded mode and restores normal operation.

### 5.5.3 Pool allocation

Memory for the shared pool is allocated by SGLang, not by the storage server. SGLang has direct knowledge of NUMA topology and page alignment requirements that the storage server does not possess. Letting SGLang own the allocation keeps those decisions local to the component that understands them.

The alternative, i.e. the storage server allocates memory and shares it back to SGLang, creates a complicated lifecycle problem.  The storage server has to maintain memory between restarts, e.g. keep mmaped file in `/dev/shm`, which adds more difficulties to implementation of a storage server.

---

## 6. Prototype

Here is a vibe-coding demo, for proof-of-concept only.

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24543

### Related resources

_No response_

title: RFC: migrate deepseek_vl2 vision tower from timm to transformers SiglipVisionModel
author: 1fanwang
body:
## Context

`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_vl2.py:_init_vision_module` carries a TODO since at least 0.5.x:

```python
# TODO: refactor vision model through timm wrapper from transformers
try:
    import timm
except ImportError:
    raise ImportError("Please install timm") from None
model = timm.create_model("vit_so400m_patch14_siglip_384.webli", ...)
```

The vision tower is SigLIP SO400M-patch14-384 — public weights at `google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384`, supported in `transformers` as `SiglipVisionModel`. The timm route works but pins sglang to a third-party dep for one model variant.

Wanted to check direction before drafting code.

## Proposed shape

Replace the timm call with `transformers.SiglipVisionModel` constructed from the local config. Keep `_init_vision_module(vision_config, quant_config)` signature unchanged (currently both args are unused; preserving the signature avoids touching call sites).

Two real risks:

1. **Weight-key mapping.** The deepseek-vl2-tiny safetensors store the vision tower under timm's naming (`vision.blocks.{i}.attn.qkv.weight`, `vision.blocks.{i}.norm1.weight`, ...). `SiglipVisionModel` uses HF's naming (`vision_model.encoder.layers.{i}.self_attn.{q,k,v}_proj.weight`, `vision_model.encoder.layers.{i}.layer_norm1.weight`, ...). Need a one-shot key-rename on the safetensors load path, otherwise weights silently fail to populate.

2. **Numerical equivalence.** Need to confirm `timm.SiglipSO400M.forward_features(x) == SiglipVisionModel(x).last_hidden_state` (modulo CLS token / pooling differences) at fp32 cosine ≥ 0.9999 before flipping the load path. Easy to assume; cheap to verify.

`forward_features` returns patch-token tensors directly from timm's last block. `SiglipVisionModel` returns a `BaseModelOutputWithPooling` with `last_hidden_state` as the equivalent. Output shapes should match when initialized from the same weights, but worth a numerical check.

## Plan

1. PR 1: add a key-rename pass in the existing `load_weights` for `vision.*` keys → SiglipVisionModel layout. Keep timm load path active. Add a unit test that constructs both, runs them on the same input, asserts output cosine-similarity. Land first as a no-behavior-change verification harness.

2. PR 2: flip `_init_vision_module` to construct `SiglipVisionModel(config.vision_config)`, drop timm import. Run the same numerical test pre/post. Drop the `import timm` requirement from the model dependency surface.

3. Delete the TODO.

Step 1 lands the proof; step 2 lands the migration. Step 1 alone is useful even if step 2 stalls — gives anyone touching the vision tower a regression test for free.

## Open questions

- Is this on someone's roadmap already? Don't want to step on parallel work.
- Is the timm dep something you actually want to drop, or is it kept intentionally (e.g. easier to swap in non-HF ViT variants)?
- Any preference on landing as one PR vs. the two-step split above?

Happy to draft step 1 once direction's settled.

title: [Feature][RFC] Add `SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` for fine-grained Ray bundle index control
author: KaisennHu
body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes adding `placement_group` parameter and `SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` environment variable to enable **precise, per-worker control** over Ray placement group bundle index assignment. This allows users to customize worker placement topology, including skipping unhealthy GPUs, topology-aware scheduling, and Ray Serve Gang Scheduling integration. vLLM provides a similar feature via `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES`.

## Motivation

### Problem Statement

SGLang's Ray-based distributed execution auto-creates placement groups with one bundle per node (multiple GPUs per bundle). Users cannot override this assignment.

**Current behavior**:
```python
bundle_for_node = [engine_bundle] + [i for i in range(nnodes) if i != engine_bundle]
```

This prevents:

1. **Skipping unhealthy GPUs**: When specific GPUs are faulty, users cannot select alternative bundles
2. **Topology-aware placement**: Assigning workers to bundles with specific interconnect characteristics (NVLink vs PCIe)
3. **Ray Serve Gang Scheduling**: Integration with RLHF/RL workflows requires user-provided placement groups with per-GPU bundle granularity

### Use Cases

```bash
# Skip faulty GPUs: Use bundles 0,1,2,7 (skip 3-6) for tp_size=4
export SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES="0,1,2,7"

# Topology-aware: Place TP workers on NVLink-connected GPUs
export SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES="0,1,2,3"
```

## Proposed Solution

### Two Placement Modes

| Mode | Trigger | Bundle Structure | Bundle Assignment |
|------|---------|------------------|-------------------|
| **Auto PG** | No `placement_group` | One bundle per node, multiple GPUs | Original behavior unchanged |
| **Custom PG** | User provides `placement_group` | User-defined, exactly 1 GPU per bundle | `bundle_indices[rank]` via env var |

### Components

**`placement_group` parameter**: User-provided placement group triggers Custom PG mode.

**`SGLANG_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES` env var**: Comma-separated integers specifying bundle indices per rank (Custom PG only).

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Format | `"0,1,2,3"` |
| Length | Must equal `world_size` |
| Validation | Fail-fast on mismatch, duplicates, out-of-range |

### World Size

| Config | world_size |
|--------|------------|
| Standard | `dp_size * tp_size * pp_size` |
| enable_dp_attention=True | `tp_size * pp_size` |

## Backward Compatibility

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| No `placement_group` | Auto PG (original behavior) |
| `placement_group` + no env var | Custom PG, sequential indices `[0,1,...]` |
| `placement_group` + env var | Custom PG, user-specified indices |

## Files to Modify

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `server_args.py` | Add `placement_group` parameter |
| `engine.py` | Helper functions + Custom PG mode |
| `data_parallel_controller.py` | Import helpers + Custom PG support |

## Testing

Placement group functionality tests in `test/manual/test_ray_engine.py`.

## References

- vLLM `VLLM_RAY_BUNDLE_INDICES`: [ray_executor.py#L186-L197](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor.py#L186-L197)
- Ray Placement Groups: https://docs.ray.io/en/latest/ray-core/scheduling/placement-group.html

## CC Lists

@jeffreywang-anyscale @tianyi-ge

title: [RFC] Agent-Aware KV Cache Phase 1 for Agentic Workloads
author: stmatengss
body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes Phase 1 of agent-aware KV cache support in SGLang.

The goal of this phase is to add a minimal, backward-compatible metadata path for agentic workloads so workflow information can flow from the API layer into runtime requests and KV cache nodes, and optionally affect radix cache eviction.

This is intentionally a foundation/prototype phase, not a full workflow-aware cache system.

## Motivation

Current KV cache eviction policies such as LRU, LFU, and SLRU treat requests mostly independently. That works well for standard chat/completion workloads, but it misses reuse opportunities in agentic workflows, where requests often share:

- repeated prompt prefixes across planner/tool/worker steps
- parent/child step relationships
- short-term reuse after tool calls
- workflow-level TTL or reuse intent

Without workflow-aware signals, cache entries that are likely to be reused by upcoming steps may be evicted too early.

## Proposal

Phase 1 introduces:

- an optional `agent_hints` field in OpenAI-compatible requests
- propagation of `agent_hints` through the internal request pipeline
- lightweight workflow DAG tracking in the scheduler
- radix cache node annotation with workflow metadata
- a new optional radix eviction policy: `agent_aware`

Initial `agent_hints` fields include:

- `workflow_id`
- `agent_id`
- `step_id`
- `step_index`
- `total_steps`
- `parent_step_id`
- `children_step_ids`
- `tool_name`
- `expected_tool_duration_ms`
- `cache_ttl_ms`
- `shared_prefix_hash`
- `reuse_hint`

## Scope

Phase 1 is intended to cover:

- request schema support
- metadata plumbing
- scheduler-side workflow tracking
- cache node metadata annotation
- a prototype workflow-aware eviction strategy

Phase 1 does **not** attempt to fully solve:

- `shared_prefix_hash`-driven reuse
- HiCache / storage-layer metadata inheritance
- cross-process workflow coordination
- production-tuned scoring for all agent topologies

## Backward Compatibility

- `agent_hints` is optional
- existing clients do not need to change
- existing eviction policies continue to work unchanged
- the new behavior is opt-in

## Testing

Expected validation for Phase 1:

- schema tests for `agent_hints`
- propagation tests from API request to internal request objects
- workflow DAG tests for step registration and distance computation
- radix cache node annotation tests
- eviction ordering tests for `agent_aware`
- backward-compat tests when `agent_hints` is omitted

How to Run
Start SGLang with the new eviction policy:
```
curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
    "agent_hints": {
      "workflow_id": "wf-1",
      "agent_id": "planner",
      "step_id": "step-1",
      "children_step_ids": ["step-2"],
      "cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
      "reuse_hint": "keep"
    }
  }'
```

Prototype validation already exists with dedicated unit tests for the metadata path.

## Open Questions

- Should `shared_prefix_hash` remain a hint, or become a stronger reuse primitive in a later phase?
- Should TTL be a hard protection or only a ranking signal?
- How should workflow-aware metadata eventually interact with HiCache and storage backends?
- What observability should be added next: workflow hit rate, protected eviction count, step-distance metrics?

## Requested Feedback

Feedback is especially useful on:

- the proposed `agent_hints` schema
- whether scheduler-local DAG tracking is the right Phase 1 boundary
- whether `agent_aware` should land as an experimental eviction policy first
- what should be included in Phase 2

title: [RFC] Refactor weight loading code
author: b8zhong
body:
# Weight Loader RFC

Claude assisted, I took a pass, and most of the suggestions seem reaonsable.

This RFC describes a proposal for interfaces and abstractions for the model weight loading layer.

Today, we have 165 model files in `python/sglang/srt/models/`, each carrying its own ~50–150 line `load_weights`. The largest (`deepseek_v2.py`) is 2.4k lines. And `sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` is over 700 lines long. 

Every time someone wants to fix a behavior here, they end up touching one model and missing the rest, since the same control flow is copy-pasted across the whole directory. For examples, the following PRs are for simply adding remapping per model for NVFP4 models:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18224
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18189

But the same happens for supporting PP, etc. 

(There are more, but I cannot find them right now..)

## Motivation

The per-model `load_weights` functions repeat the same boilerplate over and over. Some quick numbers from grep today:

- 116 / 165 model files declare their own `stacked_params_mapping` (almost always the same `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` tuples).
- 83 / 165 files repeat the `rotary_emb.inv_freq` / `cos_cached` / `sin_cached` skip block verbatim.
- 27 / 165 files repeat the `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name(...)` block.
- 28 / 165 files repeat the `tie_word_embeddings` + `lm_head.weight` skip.
- 352 call sites to `is_pp_missing_parameter` / `start_layer` / `end_layer` guards, all sprinkled inside the per-model loops.

So fixes to FP8 kv-scale remapping, fused module support, or PP edge cases tend to land in one or two files and quietly miss the rest. The `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` extraction is evidence that we already feel this pain — but the pattern stops at one model family.

The control flow inside each `load_weights` is fundamentally the same procedural sweep:

```text
for name, weight in weights:
    skip rotary buffers;
    skip out-of-range PP layers;
    remap kv-scale names;
    skip lm_head if tied;
    walk stacked_params_mapping → maybe load + break;
    walk expert_params_mapping → maybe load + break;
    fall-through default_weight_loader.
```

This isn't really domain logic, it's plumbing — and it would be much nicer to have it living in one place.

For reference, vLLM solved a very similar problem with `AutoWeightsLoader` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:117`). Their `llama.py:load_weights` is 5 lines. Ours is 74 lines doing essentially the same thing.

## Proposal

### Abstraction

Three pieces, each non-intrusive:

1. **Walker** (`AutoWeightsLoader`). Given a root `nn.Module` and an iterable of `(name, tensor)`, it walks the module tree. For each child it finds, if that child has its own `load_weights`, defer to it; otherwise recurse; at the leaf, look up `param.weight_loader` (already the convention used by sglang's linear / fused MoE layers) and call it. This is where rotary skip, PP skip, kv-scale remap, tie-word-embeddings skip, and "not found" diagnostics all live exactly once.

2. **Name remapper** (`WeightsMapper`). A small declarative dataclass: `{regex|substr|prefix|suffix → new_name | None}`. Replaces the dozens of `name = name.replace("foo", "bar")` lines, plus the "set name to None to drop it" idiom. Composable via `|` so quant remaps and model remaps stack cleanly.

3. **Quirks registry**, parallel to the `OverrideRegistry` in the server-args proposal. Per-architecture hooks for things like DeepSeek's `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` (currently injected into `packed_modules_mapping` inside `__init__`) or w4afp8's expert-input-scale mapping. Today these are `if quant_config.get_name() == "w4afp8": ...` branches inside the loader; they should be registered, not branched, in the model loading code.

### Interface

After the walker is in place, a typical model's `load_weights` would look like:

```python
class LlamaForCausalLM(nn.Module):
    def load_weights(self, weights):
        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(
            self,
            skip_prefixes=["lm_head."] if self.config.tie_word_embeddings else None,
        )
        return loader.load_weights(weights)
```

That covers the 80% case. Models with real special cases override at the *module* level instead of the top-level model:

```python
class DeepseekV2MoE(nn.Module):
    def load_weights(self, weights):
        # MoE-specific expert sharding — only this submodule, not the whole model
        ...
```

The walker sees `DeepseekV2MoE.load_weights` exists and defers to it; the rest of the model still rides the auto path. This is where most of the win comes from: today, one quirk in one submodule forces you to write the entire top-level loader by hand.

```python
@WeightQuirkRegistry.register(["DeepseekV3ForCausalLM"])
def deepseek_quirks(model, mapper: WeightsMapper) -> WeightsMapper:
    if model.fuse_qkv_a_proj:
        mapper |= WeightsMapper(orig_to_new_substr={
            "q_a_proj": "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa",
            "kv_a_proj_with_mqa": "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa",
        })
    return mapper
```

Subsystem interface: nothing else in the codebase needs to know the walker exists. `model_loader/loader.py` keeps calling `model.load_weights(...)` exactly as today, and the change is local to `srt/models/*`.

## Breaking Changes

Since this is not exactly **public** API, we can maybe keep on making further changes for readability/usability/ease of maintenance. It will only affect those with out of tree models (requires them changing the mdoel code).

- Delete `stacked_params_mapping` and `packed_modules_mapping` from every model class. They move to the layer that owns the fusion. Out-of-tree models that copy-pasted these will need to drop them.
- Standardize the `load_weights` return type to `set[str]` (loaded param names). Today some return `None`, some return nothing. This unblocks "expected but missing" diagnostics in the walker.
- Delete `do_load_weights` / `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` — the walker subsumes it. Submodule-level `load_weights` overrides replace it cleanly.
- Delete `get_module_name_from_weight_name`, `get_num_params`, `get_weights_by_name` from individual model classes (used mostly by tests and weight-update RPC). These are mechanical and belong on the walker / a single helper, not duplicated per model.
- Drop the per-loop `is_pp_missing_parameter` / `start_layer` / `end_layer` checks. Make `PPMissingLayer` short-circuit traversal in the walker so model code never has to think about PP boundaries again. (~352 call sites go away.)
- Lift the `ThreadPoolExecutor` + `should_async_load` path out of the DeepSeek mixin and make it the default in the walker, so every model gets it for free. Behavior change: load order becomes non-deterministic, but `weight_loader` callers should already not depend on order.
- Standardize on `Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]` (drop the legacy `Tuple` typing, drop the variant signatures like `is_nextn=False` kwarg — the NextN distinction can be handled by a quirk that swaps in a different mapper).
- `bitsandbytes_stacked_params_mapping` becomes the same registry mechanism, not a separate per-model attribute.

These are aggressive but each one removes a category of duplication, not just lines.

## Open questions

1. Migration order. first, do the easy and less used models, we can do Deepseek files at the very end.

title: [RFC] SGLang EPD Performance / Architecture / Observability Enhancements
author: Abatom
body:
# [RFC] SGLang EPD Performance / Architecture / Observability Enhancements

## 1. Motivation

The community introduced EPD (Encoder-Prefill-Decode) disaggregation via #12263 in December 2025. We ported it into our internal fork in January 2026 (based on the v0.5.5 baseline). Since then, our team has made extensive engineering optimizations and stability fixes around EPD for MiMo-V2.5, which have been validated through long-running online inference at large-scale production. These changes have not yet been contributed back upstream — the goal of this RFC is to reintroduce these production-proven changes to the community, rewritten against the current mainline and delivered incrementally.

Over the past several months, we identified and resolved the following bottlenecks one by one:

- **Image preprocessing bottleneck**: In large-image scenarios, running resize / normalize / patchify on the CPU dominates end-to-end latency. We migrated preprocessing to the GPU to eliminate the CPU bottleneck. (The community independently implemented the same approach in #15456.)
- **High-volume image download bottleneck**: Under high QPS, images were downloaded serially one by one, and PIL decoding of large images was constrained by the GIL. We used `multiprocessing` for parallel download + PIL decode across multiple processes, bypassing the GIL. (The community implemented a similar capability in #15456 using multithreading.)
- **Serial download / forward**: Even after the two optimizations above, batches were still processed serially — while batch N was running forward, batch N+1 could only wait. We built a pipeline: multiprocess download + PIL decode → queue → GPU preprocess + ViT forward, allowing concurrent execution and cross-batch overlap.
- **Kernel launch overhead of small ViT / Audio ops**: With small batches and fixed shapes, the overhead of numerous kernel launches accounts for a significant share of runtime. We used CUDA Graph capture + replay to skip launch overhead. (The community already has a `ViTCudaGraphRunner` for the Qwen family; we extended it for MiMo ViT and added a new Audio CUDA Graph path.)
- **Redundant download + preprocessing at Decode nodes**: In EPD mode, the Decode node re-downloads images / videos / audio and re-runs the processor. We changed the flow so that after Prefill finishes, lightweight metadata is forwarded to Decode via the bootstrap server, skipping the entire download + preprocess path.

In addition, we completed work across architecture (per-process DP Encoder, SHM transport enhancements), features (automatic audio-track extraction from video, MiMo-V2.5 EPD adaptation), observability (OTel tracing, MM token propagation, `EncoderMetricsCollector`), and other optimizations (HTTP session reuse, fine-grained caching, `RadixCache.split_by_offset`, CUDA sync elimination).

**Performance gains** (standalone encoder benchmark, MiMo-V2.5, 1K-token image):

| | QPS | Avg latency | P90 latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (0.5.5) | 15 | 78.39 ms | 100.76 ms |
| After (0.5.5)  | 30 | 80.28 ms | 82.94 ms |

QPS improved **2×** with comparable latency — the gains come primarily from cross-request batching, parallel image download, download / forward pipelining, and GPU-side preprocessing. The benchmark tool has already been submitted as a standalone PR (*[Bench] Add QPS-based encoder benchmark for EPD separation* #24700 ).

## 2. PR Overview

| PR | Category | Description | PR |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | Feature | MiMo-V2.5 EPD support | #24931(merged) |
  | 2 | Feature | Automatic video audio track extraction | #24931(merged) |
  | 3 | Performance | Parallel video decoding | #25588(merged) |
  | 4 | Performance | Encoder performs image preprocessing on GPU | #25588(merged) |
  | 5 | Performance | EncoderScheduler batching | #25964(merged) |
  | 6 | Architecture | Encoder supports DP (Data Parallelism) | #26576(merged) |
  | 7 | Performance | HTTP session reuse | #28056(merged) |
  | 8 | Performance | Image download / forward pipelining | #29712 |
  | 9 | Performance | Fine-grained multimodal cache | #28435 |
  | 10 | Performance | Prefill pipelining | #26708 |
  | 11 | Performance | CUDA sync elimination | #26082(merged) |
  | 12 | Performance | MM metadata forward propagation | |

title: [RFC][Refactor] `mem_cache` pool / allocator restructure
author: alphabetc1
body:
> **Roadmap v2.** Rewritten against `sglang/main` @ 2026-08-20; the original body is
> in this issue's edit history. Hardware backends (`hardware_backend/npu/`,
> `hardware_backend/mlx/`) are **out of scope** and are not covered by any item or
> guard below.

---

## 1. TL;DR

Reorganize `mem_cache/` from "a few catch-all files plus cross-feature pollution"
into per-family one-module-per-family packages:

- `allocator.py` → `allocator/` package — **done**, keep it closed
- `memory_pool_host.py` → `pool_host/` package — **in progress**, 3 items left
- `memory_pool.py` + 6 sibling files → `pool/` package — **not started**, and it is
  the only part of `mem_cache/` still actively getting worse
- Untangle DSv4 ↔ HiSparse class misplacement
- Naming rule: **remove role affixes that don't differentiate**
- Add `mem_cache/README.md` (type × scope) index
- Land a CI guard so the layout cannot regress once a target directory exists

---

## 2. Why v2: what changed since the RFC was opened

The RFC was opened 2026-05-15. Three months of data:

| File | 2026-05-15 | 2026-08-20 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `memory_pool.py` | 2257 lines / 11 classes | **5042 lines / 17 classes** | **+123%** |
| `memory_pool_host.py` | 2105 lines / 8 classes | **1517 lines / 6 classes** | −28% |

The layer that got a target directory shrank. The layer that did not got 2.8k lines
and 6 new classes dumped into it: `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`, `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`,
`MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool`, `DSATokenToKVPool`, plus `KVWriteLoc` /
`KvBufferDesc`.

Two consequences drive v2:

1. **`pool/` moves from last to first.** It is the only remaining catch-all and the
   only one still growing.
2. **A directory alone is not a rule.** #29678 (2026-07-01) added
   `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559 lines, 3 allocator classes) at top level *two
   months after* `allocator/` existed. Section 8 adds the guard.

Additional drift the original body does not reflect:

- `unified_cache_components/` was moved to `unified_cache/components/` in 60d6914f1
  (2026-07-28), but the `_component` suffix was kept. The naming rule was silently
  dropped; the tree in the old §3.2 is contradicted by a landed PR.
- `NSATokenToKVPool` → `DSATokenToKVPool`; `NSAIndexerPoolHost` → `DSAIndexerPoolHost`.
  All `nsa` names in the old tree are stale.
- `allocator/mamba.py` holds `MambaSlotAllocator`, not `MambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator`.
- `allocator/swa.py` gained `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` — filed correctly, which
  is the evidence that the rule works once the directory exists.
- New, entirely uncovered by the old roadmap: `unified_memory_pool.py` (1691),
  `multi_ended_allocator.py` (2559), `kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190),
  `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `index_key_cache.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`,
  `mamba_slot_fused.py`, `kv_vmm_backing.py`, `layout/`, `buffer_mode/`,
  `allocation.py`, `allocation_sizing.py`, `embedding_store.py`.

---

## 3. Rules for every PR under this issue

1. Title must carry the `[mem_cache][N/N]` prefix and state whether it is a
   **Mechanical Move**.
2. Mechanical Moves must satisfy the `mechanical-refactor-verify` skill.
3. Preserve git blame as far as possible; `git blame -C -C` is the accepted fallback.
4. **No compatibility shims.** Each move updates all importers in the same PR. This
   is the established precedent — `allocator.py` was deleted outright, not left as a
   re-export. `memory_pool.py` currently has 98 importers; they get updated, not
   forwarded.
5. Every PR must shrink the guard allowlist (§8) by exactly the classes it moved.
6. Adequate test coverage, and detailed review — no exceptions for "trivial" moves.

---

## 4. Naming rules

1. **Drop role affixes that do not differentiate.** If every file in a directory
   shares the role the directory already names, the affix carries no information:
   `pool_host/mha.py`, not `pool_host/mha_pool_host.py`. Keep `_backend` /
   `_controller` style only where same-directory siblings have *different* roles.
2. **A family is a module, and a module may be a file or a package.** One file per
   family is the default; a family over ~1500 lines becomes a package
   (`pool/deepseek_v4/` already does this, and `pool/mha/` must — see §5).
3. `Allocator` is overloaded and the two meanings must not be merged:
   - **slot allocator** — a `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` subclass, answers
     "which slots are free". These belong in `allocator/`.
   - **host tensor allocator** — `HostTensorAllocator` and its subclasses
     (`ShmHostTensorAllocator`, `MooncakeHostTensorAllocator`,
     `UMBPHostTensorAllocator`), answers "give me pinned host memory". These stay in
     `pool_host/common.py` and `storage/`, and are **not** in scope for `allocator/`.

---

## 5. Target tree

```
mem_cache/
├── README.md                             # (type × scope) index
│
├── allocator/                            # slot indexing — CLOSED except for the two items in §6.1
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── base.py                           # BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator (abc only)
│   ├── token.py                          # TokenToKVPoolAllocator (page_size=1)
│   ├── paged.py                          # PagedTokenToKVPoolAllocator
│   ├── mamba.py                          # MambaSlotAllocator
│   ├── swa.py                            # SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
│   │                                     # PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
│   ├── hisparse.py                       # HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator
│   │                                     # DeepSeekV4HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator
│   └── multi_ended.py                    # MultiEndedAllocator
│                                         # UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator
│                                         # UnifiedSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator
│
├── pool/                                 # device physical storage
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── base.py                           # KVCache + BaseSWAKVPool + KVWriteLoc + KvBufferDesc
│   ├── req_to_token.py                   # ReqToTokenPool + HybridReqToTokenPool
│   ├── mha/                              # 6 classes / ~1900 lines → package
│   │   ├── __init__.py

Deleted when their last class moves out: `memory_pool.py`, `memory_pool_host.py`,
`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `deepseek_v4_compress_state.py`, `swa_memory_pool.py`,
`base_swa_memory_pool.py`, `hisparse_memory_pool.py`, `unified_memory_pool.py`,
`multi_ended_allocator.py`, `mamba_checkpoint_pool.py`, `dsa_cache_layer_split.py`,
`index_key_cache.py`.

---

## 6. Roadmap

      *(this was missed by #32484, which moved the directory but kept the suffixes)*

### 6.5 Documentation and guard

- [x] `mem_cache/README.md` — layer map, placement-by-base-class, §4 naming rules,
      §7 dependency invariants — #35643. Deliberately coarse: a per-class inventory
      would need updating by every remaining move, and it already has a rot-proof
      home in §8's shrink-only pins.

      (allocator + pool_host), R2, R3, R4 — #35638 (draft, stacked on #35306)

      `.claude/rules/modify-component-must-read.md`

---

## 7. Layering and dependency invariants

```
        scheduler / model_runner / attention backend
