```
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  hybrid_cache/                           │  multi-pool router
        └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │
                          ▼
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │  allocator/                              │  "give me N slots"
        └──────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          │ holds a reference to ↓
                          ▼
        ┌────────────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────┐
        │  pool/  (device, L1)   │ ─ hicache ►│  pool_host/  (host, L2)  │
        └────────────────────────┘  offload   └──────────────────────────┘
                                                          │
                                                          ▼
                                              ┌──────────────────────────┐
                                              │  storage/  (L3)          │
                                              └──────────────────────────┘

    construction layer (cuts across all of the above, not a tier):
      kv_cache_configurator.py, kv_cache_builder.py, cache_init_params.py,
      allocation_sizing.py, kv_cache_dtype.py, kv_vmm_backing.py,
      hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py
```

| Module | Cares about | In → Out |
|---|---|---|
| `allocation.py` | per-batch allocation policy | `batch` → `out_cache_loc` |
| `hybrid_cache/` | per-layer routing across pools | `layer_id` → pool |
| `allocator/` | which slots are free | `need_size` → `indices` |
| `pool/` | physical KV / SSM state layout | `(layer_id, indices) ↔ tensor` |
| `pool_host/` | host mirror + H2D/D2H | `device_indices ↔ host_indices` |

**Dependency invariants** (machine-checkable, enforced by §8):

- `pool/` must not import `allocator/`, `hybrid_cache/`, or `allocation.py`.
- `pool_host/` must not import `allocator/` or `hybrid_cache/`.
- `allocator/` may import `pool/` (it holds the pool it allocates into); the reverse
  is forbidden.
- Nothing under `pool/`, `pool_host/`, or `allocator/` may import the construction
  layer. Construction depends on them, never the other way round.

The original RFC declared per-layer responsibilities but no dependency direction.
Without an enforced direction, the split only relocates files — the layers stop being
layers the first time a pool reaches back up into an allocator.

---

## 8. Guard: `test_mem_cache_layout_ratchet.py`

A directory is not a rule (see §2). The guard is a ratchet test in
`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`, modelled on the existing
`test/registered/unit/test_module_state_ratchet.py` and registered into
`base-a-test-cpu`. Four pins, each shrink-only, each covering one way the layout
regressed after the restructure was agreed.

### R1 — a class lives where its base class says

**Role is decided by base class, never by class name** — `HostTensorAllocator` is
named `Allocator` but hands out pinned host memory, not KV slots (§4.3). Because
inheritance crosses modules, the test builds a class graph over `mem_cache/` and takes
its transitive closure. Class names do collide (three modules define `TreeNode`), so
ancestry is unioned across same-named definitions: over-approximating turns a
collision into a review conversation, where dropping all but one definition would turn
it into a silent miss.

| Transitive base | Required home |
|---|---|
| `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` | `mem_cache/allocator/` |
| `HostKVCache` | `mem_cache/pool_host/` |
| `KVCache`, `BaseSWAKVPool`, `ReqToTokenPool`, `MambaPool` | `mem_cache/pool/` *(deferred)* |

`_LEGACY_HOMES` pins the five classes still misfiled today (3 allocators in
`multi_ended_allocator.py`, 2 host pools in `memory_pool_host.py`).

**The pool role is enforced only once `mem_cache/pool/` exists.** An error telling
someone to file a class into a package nobody has created is a trap, not a rule. R3
covers the device pools in the meantime; when the first `pool/` PR lands, `pool` joins
the enforced roles and its 29 classes move from R3's pin into `_LEGACY_HOMES`.

### R2 — no new top-level modules

`_TOP_LEVEL_MODULES` freezes the 40 `mem_cache/*.py` files that exist today. A new
top-level module must go into a package, or grow the pin in the same PR — which forces
the "why is this not in a package?" conversation into review instead of leaving it to
be noticed three months later.

### R3 — modules slated for deletion only shrink

R1 and R2 both miss the most damaging case: a class appended to a module that already
exists. That is exactly how `memory_pool.py` gained `PageMajorMHATokenToKVPool`,
`MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`, `MHATokenToKOnlyPool`, `MiniMaxSparseKVPool` and
`DSATokenToKVPool` after the split was agreed.

`_SHRINKING_MODULES` pins the class list of every module §5 marks for deletion. It
needs no target package to exist, so it is what stands in for the pool role until R1
takes over.

### R4 — layers don't import upwards

Asserts the §7 dependency invariants over the import graph. It passes on `main` today,
so it locks in a property the code already has rather than demanding new work.

### Mechanics

- Pins hold today's state, so the test is green on landing and never blocks unrelated
  work.
- A violation that is not pinned → fail, with an error naming the correct target file
  and linking this roadmap.
- **Every pin also fails when it rots**: a class that has moved, a module that is gone,
  a file that no longer exists. This makes every move PR shrink a pin (Rule 5 in §3)
  and turns the pins into the migration's progress ledger.
- Scope is `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` only. `hardware_backend/` is explicitly
  excluded — its NPU/MLX pools and allocators are a separate device axis and are not
  governed by this issue.

Each of the six failure paths (four violations, two rot cases) was verified to fire by
injecting the violation into a scratch copy of the tree; a guard nobody has seen go red
is not a guard.

A skill (`.claude/skills/mem-cache-layout/SKILL.md`) covers the same rules for coding
agents, but is *not* the guard: human PRs never read `.claude/skills/`. The ratchet
blocks; the skill only teaches.

---

## 9. Resolved design decisions

**D1 — `Unified*` shared-arena classes stay cohesive.**
`unified_memory_pool.py` and `multi_ended_allocator.py` (both from #29678) are
`Unified*` variants of every family, but they are coupled to a shared `UnifiedKVPool`
arena rather than to their own families. Folding each into its family file would
spread one concern across six files. They keep their cohesion in `pool/unified/` and
`allocator/multi_ended.py`, as §5 shows. `pool/unified/` is the one place where the
one-module-per-family rule (§4.2) is deliberately overridden by a
one-module-per-arena split.

**D2 — the construction layer is a follow-up issue, not part of this one.**
`kv_cache_configurator.py` (2190) + `kv_cache_builder.py` + `cache_init_params.py` +
`allocation_sizing.py` + `kv_cache_dtype.py` + `kv_vmm_backing.py` +
`hybrid_cache/pool_assembler.py` (1960) is ~5.5k lines with no home in the tier
diagram. §7 recognizes it as a cross-cutting layer; §5 deliberately leaves the files
where they are. `mem_cache/build/` gets planned as its own issue **after §6.3 lands** —
moving construction and storage in the same window would churn the same importers
twice and make every Mechanical Move proof harder to review.

**D3 — `IndexKeyCache` goes into `pool/dsa.py`, with no new base class.**
Its only two importers are `DSATokenToKVPool` and `LayerSplitIndexKeyCache`, both of
which land in `pool/dsa.py`; it holds a `self.pool` back-reference and reads ten pool
attributes, so today the two sides only avoid an import cycle via `TYPE_CHECKING` and
a string annotation. Same module removes the cycle. Its whole API (`move`,
`get_buffer`, `store_quantized`, `cpu_copy`, `load_cpu_copy`, `state_buf_infos`) is
the storage contract, and `DSATokenToKVPool` forwards to it one line at a time — it is
simply DSA's second device buffer.

It is **not** given a `KVCache` base just so the guard can classify it: inventing an
abstraction to satisfy a linter is the wrong direction. Rule 2 of §8 covers it
instead, by pinning the top-level module list.

title: [RFC] Streaming API for Real-Time Server State and Metrics
author: liu-cong
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

### Motivation.

Distributed inference routers (e.g., `llm-d-router`) require real-time visibility into engine capacity to balance load effectively. Current scraping/polling methods (like Prometheus `/metrics` pulling) introduce dual inefficiencies:
1. **Latency & Staleness:** A single large request can instantly saturate a server. Routing layers remain blind to this during the polling window, sending subsequent traffic that causes cascading queuing delays or OOMs.
2. **Resource Waste:** Continuous HTTP requests occur even when the server state is completely static.

While routers try to mitigate this by estimating in-flight load locally, this state is fragile across router restarts and lacks accurate engine-level visibility into metrics like dynamic KV-cache occupancy.

### Proposed Change.

Expose an optional **streaming API endpoint** (e.g.,  `grpc` streaming) from the engine allowing routers to establish a persistent connection. The model server will asynchronously push structured metrics the moment internal scheduling states change, reducing telemetry lag down to network transport latency.

The detailed design will be updated later.

### Related resources

A similar RFC was submitted to vllm as well https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43643
