#24542 proposed a standalone storage process using UDS/gRPC for control and shared `memfd` host memory for the bulk data path.

Its central principle is similar:

```text
control plane -> descriptors
data plane    -> shared memory
```

This RFC asks whether that process boundary could move one tier closer to the accelerator:

```text
#24542

SGLang HiCache
    │
shared host memory
    ▼
Standalone L3 StorageServer


This proposal

SGLang scheduler
    │
device-memory IPC
(CUDA IPC initially)
    ▼
HiCacheDaemon
    ├── Host tier
    └── L3 storage
```

#### #32710 — Rust TreeCore

The merged Rust TreeCore work makes the tree/data-plane boundary more explicit.

One possible architecture is:

```text
Scheduler
    ├── scheduling
    ├── Rust TreeCore
    └── GPU allocator
             │
      device-memory IPC
       (CUDA initially)
             │
             ▼
       HiCacheDaemon
             ├── transfer engine
             ├── host tier
             └── external storage
```

This could keep the latency-sensitive metadata path in-process while moving bulk cache operations out of the scheduler. A future daemon-owned TreeCore design could be considered separately if cross-scheduler authoritative metadata becomes a goal.

#### #35648 — shared KV pool with CUDA IPC

#35648 explores cross-process KV sharing with a CUDA-IPC-visible physical KV allocation.

Although its goal is different (same-GPU model replicas), it highlights many of the same systems questions:

* ownership;
* publication;
* generations;
* reference lifetime;
* synchronization;
* failure recovery.

This proposal focuses specifically on the HiCache transfer/data plane rather than cross-scheduler shared prefix ownership.

### TreeCore placement

There are at least two plausible designs:

```text
A. Scheduler-local TreeCore

Scheduler
├── TreeCore
├── GPU allocator
└── execution
       │
       ▼
HiCacheDaemon
├── host tier
├── transfer
└── L3
```

This minimizes scheduler-path IPC and keeps request/cache coordination in one process.

A more aggressive design is:

```text
B. Daemon-owned TreeCore

Scheduler A ─┐
Scheduler B ─┼──► HiCacheDaemon
Scheduler C ─┘      ├── TreeCore
                    ├── cache directory
                    ├── residency
                    └── transfer
```

This could provide a single authoritative cache index across multiple schedulers, but it would also move prefix matching, locking, insertion, and potentially eviction decisions across an IPC boundary and turn more of request/cache coordination into a distributed state machine.

For a first experiment, scheduler-local TreeCore seems like the smaller correctness surface. I would still like maintainer feedback on whether that is the right long-term boundary.

### Potential benefits

If this architecture works well, possible benefits include:

* less cache I/O and transfer concurrency inside scheduler processes;
* independent HiCache lifecycle and observability;
* centralized transfer batching and bandwidth control;
* cleaner storage-backend integration;
* easier experimentation with alternative data-plane implementations;
* isolation of storage or transfer failures from scheduler logic;
* a clearer separation between cache semantics and cache movement;
* potentially reusable local cache infrastructure across inference processes.

### Costs and risks

There are also meaningful costs:

* IPC/control-message overhead;
* device-memory IPC mapping and synchronization lifecycle complexity;
* harder crash cleanup;
* host-residency metadata synchronization;
* daemon accelerator-context overhead;
* additional deployment complexity;
* possible synchronization stalls if the protocol is poorly designed;
* hardware/platform differences in memory IPC and inter-process event support.

LMCache MP's experience also suggests that stale IPC mappings, worker death, event lifetime, and cleanup behavior need explicit design and testing rather than being treated as edge cases.

### Possible minimal prototype

Instead of moving all HiCache functionality at once, a useful first experiment might only support:

* NVIDIA CUDA / Linux;
* one scheduler process;
* one local daemon;
* one GPU;
* Full attention only;
* GPU <-> host backup and restore;
* CUDA IPC as the initial device-memory IPC backend;
* scheduler-owned GPU allocator;
* scheduler-local TreeCore;
* no external L3 initially.

The goal would be to compare:

```text
current in-process HiCache transfer path

vs.

scheduler
   │
CUDA IPC
   ▼
standalone HiCacheDaemon
```

while keeping cache semantics unchanged.

Useful measurements would include:

* TTFT;
* ITL impact;
* backup/load latency;
* scheduler CPU time;
* transfer throughput;
* overlap with model execution;
* IPC/control overhead;
* GPU/host memory overhead;
* behavior under scheduler and daemon failure.

### Questions for maintainers

I would especially appreciate feedback on the following:

1. Does an out-of-process HiCache **data plane** look like a useful architectural direction for SGLang?

2. Should `UnifiedRadixCache` / TreeCore remain scheduler-local initially, or should daemon-owned TreeCore be considered from the start?

3. Should the scheduler continue to own the GPU KV allocator, with the daemon only importing its allocations through a device-memory IPC backend (CUDA IPC on NVIDIA initially)?

4. Should the host KV pool and host-tier allocator move into the daemon, or remain scheduler-owned initially?

5. What should be authoritative for host-tier residency / eviction metadata?

6. Should device-memory sharing and cross-process synchronization be modeled as separate platform capabilities, rather than assuming CUDA IPC + CUDA event IPC semantics?

7. Should one daemon serve one scheduler, one GPU, or potentially multiple scheduler processes on the same node?

8. Would an NVIDIA GPU <-> host-only prototype be a useful first step before integrating other device IPC backends and existing HiCache L3 backends?

The intent of this RFC is to discuss the **process boundary, ownership model, portability boundary, and failure semantics first**, rather than proposing an immediate large HiCache refactor.

---

### Related resources

* SGLang #24542 — `[RFC] [HiCache] A new backend for external L3 storage systems`
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24542

* SGLang #32710 — `[Radix Cache] Add Rust TreeCore backend with shared parity tests`
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32710

* SGLang #35648 — `[Feature] [RFC] Same-GPU model replicas with managed CUDA MPS and a shared KV pool`
  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35648

* LMCache multiprocess mode / `LMCacheMPConnector`
  https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/docs/source/getting_started/quickstart.rst

* LMCache SGLang multiprocess adapter
  https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/blob/dev/lmcache/integration/sglang/multi_process_adapter.py

* AMD HIP IPC APIs (`hipIpcGetMemHandle`, `hipIpcOpenMemHandle`, event IPC)
  https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/HIP/en/latest/doxygen/html/group___device.html

* Intel Level Zero IPC memory handles
  https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/EXT_IPC_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE.html

title: [RFC][Feature] Extract an In-Process Route Planner from experimental/sgl-router's PD Workflow
author: tonyluj
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Summary

The chat-completions handler currently owns both worker selection and the Prefill/Decode (PD) request lifecycle. Candidate filtering, policy selection, Decode affinity, bootstrap injection, dual dispatch, and response streaming are therefore changed and tested together.

This RFC proposes a small, behavior-preserving refactor:

1. Add an in-process `RoutePlanner` that produces the current Plain or PD route plan.
2. Move bootstrap and PD execution into a focused `PdWorkflow`.

The first milestone keeps one binary and the existing registry, policies, health/load state, API, metrics, and deployment model. It adds no scheduler service or network protocol. Reservation, feedback, and remote scheduling require separate RFCs.

This follows Step 4 of the [lightweight SessionAware Router roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760):
generate a route plan, then inject bootstrap metadata and forward both PD legs.

## Current State and Problem

The current path is:

```text
parse model
  -> resolve Plain/Prefill candidates and model policy
  -> prepare tokens/routing signals
  -> select Plain/Prefill with Policy::select
  -> select Decode with a separate affinity helper
  -> create guards, inject bootstrap fields, and dispatch
  -> return the Decode response
```

The chat handler owns most of this flow
([`chat.rs`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/experimental/sgl-router/src/server/routes/chat.rs#L111-L506)).
Prefill uses `Policy::select`
([`policies/mod.rs`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/mod.rs#L258-L280)),
while Decode uses a PD-specific same-host/min-load helper
([`policies/registry.rs`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/experimental/sgl-router/src/policies/registry.rs#L185-L285)).

This causes three practical problems:

- route-plan construction has no single owner;
- PD protocol and lifecycle tests require the large HTTP handler;
- policy and workflow changes unnecessarily expand each other's review surface.

This RFC improves ownership and testability. It does not claim a routing-quality or
throughput improvement.

## Goals

- Put pool resolution, existing policy invocation, and existing Decode affinity behind one in-process route-planning boundary.
- Put bootstrap injection and PD execution behind one workflow boundary.
- Preserve current routing, errors, cancellation, streaming, metrics, and load-guard behavior.
- Add focused tests and benchmarks without adding a network hop or background service.
- Deliver the change in small, reviewable PRs.

## Non-goals

- A scheduler process, RPC/protobuf API, or new deployment component.
- Reservations, leases, topology epochs, or a scheduling feedback protocol.
- Changes to discovery, `WorkerRegistry`, circuit breakers, or load-state ownership.
- New Prefill/Decode policies, retry behavior, or cancellation semantics.
- Multi-router HA, sticky/cache-state replication, or a shared SMG scheduling crate.
- The complete migration plan from `sgl-model-gateway`.

## Proposed Design

### Ownership

| Component | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `RoutePlanner` | Pool resolution, eligibility, existing policy invocation, Decode affinity |
| `PdWorkflow` | Bootstrap fields, both dispatches, response handling, guard lifetimes |
| Handler | Parsing, request-derived scheduling inputs, final response/access metrics |
| Proxy | Existing upstream HTTP I/O and breaker recording |
| Registry/policies | Existing membership, health/load state, and algorithms |

`RoutePlanner` means Router-side worker placement, not the scheduler inside an SGLang Engine.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H["HTTP handler"] --> P["RoutePlanner::prepare"]
    P --> I["Prepare tokens and routing signals"]
    I --> R["PlanningScope::plan"]
    R --> Q{"RoutePlan"}
    Q -->|Plain| X["Existing Plain path"]
    Q -->|Prefill + Decode| W["PdWorkflow"]
    W --> T["Proxy / engines"]
```

### Route-planning boundary

The API is crate-internal and intentionally close to the current implementation:

```rust
pub enum RoutePlan {
    Plain(DispatchTarget),
    PrefillDecode {
        prefill: DispatchTarget,
        decode: DispatchTarget,
    },
}

impl RoutePlanner {
    pub fn prepare(&self, model: &ModelId)
        -> Result<PlanningScope, RoutePlanError>;
}

impl PlanningScope {
    pub fn needs_request_tokens(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn plan(
        self,
        selection: &SelectionContext<'_>,
    ) -> Result<RoutePlan, RoutePlanError>;
}
```

`prepare` resolves the current candidates and model policy before tokenization or the external prefix-index query. This preserves today's error ordering and exposes
`needs_request_tokens` without making the handler access `PolicyRegistry`.
`plan` then calls the existing policy and, for PD, the existing Decode-affinity helper.

`DispatchTarget` is an opaque, capability-limited wrapper over the existing
`Arc<Worker>`. It exposes only identity, endpoint/bootstrap data, and the dispatch/guard capabilities needed by the workflow. It is not a wire DTO or a new state snapshot.

`RoutePlanError` maps one-to-one to current `ApiError` variants. A concrete planner is preferred initially; a trait is added only if workflow tests demonstrate a need for a fake.

### PD workflow boundary

`PdWorkflow::execute` receives a PD plan and an owned `PreparedChatRequest`. The request bundle carries the existing model, headers, original body, optional parsed JSON value, forward input IDs, Prefill load, streaming flag, and start time.

The workflow:

- derives the current bootstrap host/optional port and allocates the current 63-bit room;
- applies `input_ids` and bootstrap mutations in one JSON update;
- creates the current Prefill and Decode guards;
- starts detached Prefill and foreground Decode with the current concurrency model;
- returns the Decode response and preserves current streaming hooks and headers.

Request-body handling must retain these invariants:

- at most one full `serde_json::Value` parse beyond the existing minimal probe;
- at most one serialization when fields are injected;
- unchanged original bytes for a Plain request with no injection;
- no recomputation or clone of prepared input IDs.

The canonical HTTP fields are the optional top-level
[`bootstrap_host`, `bootstrap_port`, and `bootstrap_room`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py#L379-L385).
The Engine accepts scalar/list values and expands a scalar room to `room + i` for a batch ([`io_struct.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L826-L848)).
This RFC keeps the current missing-port value (`null`) and host fallback; it adds no
endpoint validation.

Suggested dependency direction:

```text
handler -> RoutePlanner -> WorkerRegistry / PolicyRegistry
handler -> PdWorkflow -> Proxy
PdWorkflow -X-> candidate filtering or policies
RoutePlanner -X-> bootstrap, HTTP dispatch, or streaming
```

## Compatibility Requirements

The extraction must keep the existing CLI, discovery, OpenAI-compatible schema, bootstrap fields, response headers, status/error codes, Prometheus names and labels, readiness behavior, and process count.

The following current behavior is the compatibility baseline:

| Area | Behavior to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Selection | Same candidate lists, policy instances, Decode affinity, error ordering, and no-worker/no-Prefill/no-Decode errors |
| Bootstrap/body | Same host fallback, optional port including `null`, room generation, and identical fields on both legs |
| Prefill | Detached result is not client-facing; 2xx/4xx record breaker success, 5xx records failure, and transport/timeout/body errors follow current warning/failure behavior |
| Buffered Decode | Return upstream status/body, force `application/json`, and keep current 4xx-success/5xx-failure breaker classification |
| Streaming Decode | Use `text/event-stream` on success; preserve upstream content type for error responses; a post-header failure remains a body-stream error |
| Cancellation | Stale cancellation only races upstream headers; client disconnect stops Decode but does not stop detached Prefill while the Router remains alive |
| Shutdown/retry | No detached-Prefill drain guarantee across Router shutdown and no new retry |
| Load/metrics | Weighted active load remains Prefill-only; Decode keeps its `Worker::LoadGuard`; current worker metric labels and lifetimes remain unchanged |

Some entries may be existing defects or future design choices. They are pinned only to keep this refactor behavior-preserving.

## Implementation Plan

### PR 0: Characterization and baseline

- Cover pool isolation, errors, policy/affinity behavior, bootstrap fields, PD failures, streaming, stale requests, client disconnect, guard lifetimes, and shutdown.
- Inventory existing tests first and add only missing cases.
- Record the existing `policy_select` benchmark and add Plain/PD route-planning baselines.
- Do not change production behavior.

### PR 1: Route planner

- Add `RoutePlanner`, `PlanningScope`, `DispatchTarget`, `RoutePlan`, and typed errors.
- Move the existing resolution/selection sequence behind the two-phase API.
- Make the handler consume `RoutePlan`.
- Demonstrate routing and benchmark parity.

### PR 2: PD workflow

- Move bootstrap/body mutation, dual dispatch, response handling, and guards into
  `PdWorkflow`.
- Add focused workflow tests with stub transport.
- Preserve the public API, metrics, and detached-Prefill behavior.

Follow-ups such as independent Decode policy, select-and-reserve, per-leg feedback, or a remote scheduler require separate proposals and evidence.

## Validation and Performance

- Run affected Rust unit/component/proxy suites, formatting/lints, and available Python router smoke tests. Each PR lists exact commands and blocked checks using the PR template.
- Add a route-planning Criterion benchmark covering resolver lookup, policy lookup,
  selection, Decode affinity, and plan construction for Plain/PD at representative worker counts. The existing `policy_select` benchmark remains the algorithm-only baseline.
- Compare buffered and streaming stub-worker overhead before and after workflow extraction. Report environment, commits, samples, and noise. A stable regression above 5% requires explanation and maintainer approval.
- Never dual-evaluate old/new paths on shared stateful policies. Use isolated equal-state fixtures; seed randomness where practical, otherwise verify legality and distribution.

No new production metric is required. Existing names, labels, and cardinality remain unchanged.

## Rollout, Rollback, and Risks

No feature flag or data migration is needed. Merge only after each stage passes its
characterization and performance checks. Roll back in reverse dependency order: PR 2 returns workflow code to the handler; PR 1 returns selection to the handler.

The main risks are hidden behavior drift, a hot-path regression, and an abstraction that outlives its need. Tests land first, the first implementation remains concrete, and this RFC adds no allocation protocol, network hop, or new runtime owner.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep or only reorganize the handler:** lower short-term churn, but no testable ownership boundary.
- **Reuse an SMG crate:** SMG is a useful semantic reference, but a runtime dependency would couple the lightweight replacement to the deprecated stack and broaden this RFC.
- **Add a generic or remote scheduler now:** capabilities, leases, RPC, HA, security, and versioning are not required for this extraction and need separate evidence.

cc @hzh0425 @Kangyan-Zhou @slin1237 @ByronHsu 


### Related resources

- [Lightweight SessionAware Router roadmap #25760](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)
- [RFC: Engine load reporting and Router load monitoring #32925](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32925)
- [Router-side Engine load monitoring PR #32927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/32927)
- [Per-scheduler load publication PR #34608](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34608)
- [Process-local KV indexer integration PR #33370](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33370)
- [Split PD load balancing from cache-affinity routing #26066](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/26066)
- [Decode affinity metric bug #32752](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/32752)
- [SGLang Router Architecture Improvement Proposal #7532](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/7532)
- [`sgl-model-gateway` HTTP PD router](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/sgl-model-gateway/src/routers/http/pd_router.rs#L365-L520)
- [`experimental/sgl-router` benchmarks](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8a191554e379741048ecfac02cea334eb2b883e0/experimental/sgl-router/BENCHMARKS.md)
- [SGLang contribution guide](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html)

title: [RFC] Incremental test cleanup, CI taxonomy, and shared diffusion dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
# Status update (2026-09-02)

The implementation is now consolidated in **#37436**. The former three-PR sequence (#37428, #37429, and #37433) has been folded into that PR and is superseded.

This revision narrows the RFC to what the implementation actually delivers. In particular, the 65K-line audit screening set is a review queue, not a deletion target, and the original estimates for a full hardware-directory dissolution, complete diffusion-tree move, and ~110 device-hour reduction are not claims made by #37436.

# Summary

At the August 2026 snapshot, `test/` had grown from 46,581 lines / 228 files to 504,833 lines / 2,123 files in twelve months. A second package-local tree under `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/` had reached 73,054 lines / 252 files. The growth created three related problems:

1. low-signal and duplicated tests consume review and maintenance capacity;
2. the flat registered-test layout mixes test kind, subsystem, hardware, and cadence;
3. diffusion uses a separate discovery/dispatch layer and is outside some registered-test guardrails.

The accepted direction is incremental:

- delete only candidates with file-level evidence that no maintained regression escapes;
- encode test kind in new registered paths while migrating old paths in reviewable tranches;
- keep hardware in `register_{cuda,amd,npu,xpu,mlx,musa}_ci(...)`, not in copied backend-independent scenarios;
- admit expensive or temporary CI coverage only with explicit rationale;
- share the public CI discovery/dispatch entry point with diffusion without discarding its case-aware partitioner.

# Implemented in #37436

The consolidated diff changes **197 files**, with **2,223 additions and 14,658 deletions (net -12,435 lines)**.

## 1. Evidence-based cleanup

- Removes archived manual files, permanently disabled tests, exact/AST-equivalent duplicates, shadowed tests, source-shape ratchets, static registry/export mirrors, and weak-oracle tests.
- Trims low-signal assertions from retained LLM, gateway, and diffusion suites.
- Preserves numerical/reference parity, model loading, quantization, API behavior, scheduler/cache state, distributed behavior, and hardware-specific coverage unless an equal or stronger active test exists.
- Repairs the tensor-dump forward-hook test instead of deleting it.
- Adds `scripts/lint/audit_test_value.py` and a reproducible candidate CSV.

The final B/C audit screening union is **158 files / 65,084 LOC / 2,357 cases**. This inventory is deliberately not auto-deleted. Mock-heavy tests can still protect real control flow, error handling, ownership, or state transitions.

## 2. Backend deduplication and CI admission

- Consolidates duplicated Ascend OpenAI function-calling coverage into the shared test while retaining all 12 active NPU methods and NPU-specific configuration.
- Removes AMD registrations from backend-independent API/control-plane tests.
- Removes a disabled aggregate Grok accuracy suite whose maintained model-specific replacements are active.
- Moves two high-cost, low-frequency scenarios from the default PR lane to `extra-a`.
- Adds an incremental admission checker for newly added or modified registration/skip calls:
  - temporary `disabled=` or unconditional skip requires an issue and `until YYYY-MM-DD`;
  - mixed CUDA/accelerator registration requires a nearby `backend-specific:` explanation;
  - a default PR registration above 1,200 weighted accelerator-seconds requires `ci-cost-override:` or an extra/nightly lane.

The checker is line-incremental. It does not turn pure renames or untouched legacy registrations into a flag-day failure.

## 3. Incremental kind-first taxonomy

New or moved registered tests use:

```text
test/registered/<kind>/<subsystem>/test_*.py
```

where `<kind>` is `unit`, `kernel`, `e2e`, `accuracy`, `perf`, or `stress`.

#37436 moves 64 unambiguous files with `git mv`:

- 40 model E2E files to `e2e/models`;
- 16 large-model files to `e2e/models_large`;
- 2 eval files to `accuracy/models`;
- 2 scheduled performance files to `perf/models`;
- 4 stress files to `stress/models`.

The incremental taxonomy contracts are:

| kind | enforced contract for new/moved files |
|---|---|
| `unit` | CPU-only, `est_time <= 60`, no server launch |
| `kernel` | kernel suite |
| `e2e` | registered end-to-end scenario |
| `accuracy` / `perf` | nightly or weekly cadence |
| `stress` | stress or weekly cadence |

Existing legacy paths remain valid until their subtree is migrated.

## 4. Shared diffusion CI entry point

Seven CUDA diffusion suites are registered under `test/registered/e2e/diffusion/`, and `pr-test-multimodal-gen.yml` now dispatches them through `test/run_suite.py`.

The bridge intentionally preserves diffusion's existing internals:

- case-level pytest collection;
- LPT partition plans and standalone-file estimates;
- filters and continue-on-error behavior;
- artifact paths;
- the historical `python/` working directory.

The old package-local `run_suite.py` remains a compatibility shim for callers not migrated in this tranche. The diffusion source tests are not physically moved into `test/registered/` by #37436.

# Validation evidence

- full pre-commit, syntax, registered-test, taxonomy, admission, and workflow checks pass;
- 32 checker unit tests and 35 focused diffusion bridge/partition tests pass;
- the shared runner discovers exactly the seven registered diffusion bridge files;
- on H200, the exact combined worktree runs the full diffusion unit lane through the new entry point: **2,397 passed, 107 skipped, 7 retained baseline failures, 228 subtests passed in 91.46s**;
- the retained failures are the already-known LTX2 H200 memory-policy expectation and six SM90 SubBlock CUTLASS DSL compilation failures.

# What is explicitly not part of #37436

- No automatic deletion of the 65K-line audit screening set.
- No blanket deletion of `test/manual/`.
- No complete dissolution of AMD/NPU/XPU/MUSA/MLX/CPU directories.
- No claim that 132 perf/accuracy registrations were moved or that ~110 device-hours per PR were recovered.
- No complete physical move of the diffusion test tree.
- No requirement to migrate every legacy registered path in one PR.
- No deletion quota. The cleanup stops where the remaining tests protect material correctness or hardware boundaries.

# Follow-up direction

Future cleanup or taxonomy PRs should be subtree-sized and independently reviewable. Each should include:

1. a file-level deletion/dedup rationale;
2. the stronger retained coverage that protects the same behavior;
3. before/after CI suite membership and estimated device cost when registrations change;
4. real hardware validation for kernel, distributed, model-loading, or accelerator-specific behavior;
5. exact preservation of partitioning and artifact behavior when changing a runner.

Potential follow-ups include additional hardware-independent deduplication, more kind-first `git mv` tranches, and migration of non-CUDA diffusion callers to the shared entry point. They should not be bundled into #37436 solely to reach a line-count or CI-hour target.

# Decision record

- **Implementation vehicle:** one consolidated PR, #37436.
- **Deletion policy:** human-reviewed evidence, never audit-score-only deletion.
- **Taxonomy migration:** incremental ratchet, not a flag day.
- **Diffusion integration:** shared public discovery/dispatch now; physical relocation later, if justified.
- **CI admission:** evaluate only added/modified registration or skip lines; require explicit ownership/cost rationale.
- **Review standard:** correctness and regression-gating value take precedence over code-volume targets.

title: [RFC] Quantization module layout: Config, Scheme, backend kernels
author: mmangkad
body:
## Summary

Quantization methods in SGLang are currently written in two different shapes.

Five of them follow a package layout with an explicit scheme split:

- `layers/quantization/awq/`, `compressed_tensors/`, `gptq/`, `modelslim/`, `quark/`

The rest are single files that hold config parsing, weight creation, post-load processing, and backend kernel dispatch together:

- `fp8.py` (2765 lines), `modelopt_quant.py` (3050), `mxfp4.py` (2060), and 14 smaller ones. 17 top-level files define a `QuantizationConfig` subclass today.

This RFC suggests finishing the migration so that every method follows the layout our own contribution guide already prescribes:

```text
layers/quantization/<method>/
    <method>.py          # Config: parse, validate, select a scheme
    schemes/
        <method>_linear.py   # Scheme: weight create, load, post-process
        <method>_moe.py
```

with backend kernels under `hardware_backend/<plat>/quantization/<method>_kernels.py`, and scheme selection done explicitly through `get_linear_scheme` / `get_moe_scheme`.

Nothing here is a new architecture. `docs/docs/developer_guide/quantization_contribution_guide.mdx` specifies this already, and #21126 (AWQ) and #26402 (GPTQ) are worked examples. This is a plan to take the rest of the directory there.

The intent is incremental. Every existing import path keeps working through re-export shims, each PR is small enough to review in one sitting, and the directory is busy enough that nothing should depend on a long-lived branch: it took 46, 48, 49, 56, 70 and 84 commits in the last six months, 217 in the last 90 days.

Related roadmap: #15194.

## Status

The table is meant to be updated as the series lands.

| Phase | What | PR | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Remove dead code, dedup the FP4 marlin helpers | #37552 | merged |
| 0 | Registry driven by a string spec table, lazy config resolution | #37602 | open |
| 0 | Import-shim compatibility test | #38005 | open |
| 1 | Unify the scheme ABCs in `base_scheme.py` | #38511 | open |
| 1 | Rest of shared foundations: FP8 post-load pipeline, `utils.py` split, one `is_layer_skipped`, `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`, `base_config` slimming | | planned |
| 2 | Monolith splits: `fp8`, `modelopt`, `mxfp4`, then behavioral follow-ups | | planned |
| 3 | KV-cache co-location, selection-flow tidy | | planned |
| 4 | `multimodal_gen` adapters, `inkling_common` | | planned |
| 5 | Shim removal, gated | | planned |

## Why

The current layout makes sense historically. Methods were added one at a time, each in the shape that was convenient then, and the scheme split arrived later. It is getting harder to maintain.

Some practical problems that come out of it:

- it is hard to tell where a given behavior lives, because config parsing, weight loading and kernel dispatch sit in the same 2000-line file;
- the same helper gets reimplemented per method, and the copies diverge silently. There are 11 variants of "is this layer excluded from quantization" today, and a fix applied to one copy has already failed to reach another;
- adding a method means editing an eager import block, a base dict and up to four imperative platform-override blocks, plus a separate CLI choices list. Those lists drift: until #37552 landed, `--quantization marlin` passed argparse and then failed at startup, because the choices list named a config class that was never registered;
- lists of class names maintained by hand go stale. `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED` has 20 entries, 9 of which name no class that exists;
- importing the package to ask which methods exist imports all 24 config modules, and with them every third-party quantization dependency;
- there are two separate KV-cache quantization systems (`kv_cache.py`, 83 lines, and `fp4_kv_cache_quant_method.py`, 895), and a parallel quantization stack in `multimodal_gen` (28 files, 6,620 lines) that reimplements the srt fp8, modelopt, mxfp4 and modelslim bodies while reaching into srt internals from 30 import sites;
- the four largest files are where the churn is, so unrelated changes collide in them.

For scale: 101 files, 39,262 lines.

The desired end state is simple: when someone adds or changes a quantization method, there should be one obvious file for the config, one directory for the schemes, and one line to register it.

## Proposed Shape

### Method packages

Any method with more than one scheme or backend path becomes a package, as above. Single-scheme methods can stay single files; the split is not worth it for them.

The four monoliths are the substance of the work:

| File | Lines | Becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `modelopt_quant.py` | 3050 | `modelopt/`, splitting 5 config classes from 7 method classes |
| `fp8.py` | 2765 | `fp8/` with config plus linear and MoE schemes |
| `fp8_utils.py` | 2169 | dispatch-once `Fp8LinearOp`, shared post-load helpers extracted |
| `mxfp4.py` | 2060 | `mxfp4/` with per-backend schemes |

### Registry

One declarative listing of methods, as strings, so the tables can be read without importing any config implementation:

```python
QUANTIZATION_METHOD_SPECS = {
    "fp8": "sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8:Fp8Config",
    ...
}
```

with the platform overrides as a declarative table rather than imperative `if is_npu(): BASE.update({...})` blocks, and config classes resolved on first lookup. This is what #37602 proposes; it is open, not merged, so everything described above is the state of `main` today.

### Compatibility model

The series should be conservative about anything importable:

- `sglang.srt.layers.quantization.base_config` keeps its symbols. There are 256 import statements across 251 files, plus user-facing docs teaching that path;
- the package root keeps re-exporting `QuantizationConfig`, `get_quantization_config`, `QUANTIZATION_METHODS`, and every `*Config` it exports today;
- shims are explicit re-import stubs rather than `__getattr__` indirection, so `isinstance` identity is preserved by construction and the shims stay greppable;
- shims are only removed in a final gated phase, after a release has shipped with deprecation warnings.

Some things this RFC deliberately does not propose:

- no changes to `FusedMoEMethodBase.apply` signatures or MoeRunner wiring. That migration is already in progress and marked in the code: `TODO(cwan): refactor other backends` appears in `fp8.py`, `mxfp4.py`, `quark_int4fp8_moe.py` and two MoE schemes, and `mxfp4.py:1418` notes a path that still `routes through apply without a MoeRunner`;
- no bulk relocation of kernel wrappers into `hardware_backend/`, ahead of the separate kernels-namespace work;
- no semantic merge of the two KV-cache quantization systems. They get co-located; unifying them reaches into mem_cache and the attention backends and deserves its own RFC.

### Delivery

Small PRs, titled `[N/N] Quantization Refactor: <what>`, with two rules that keep them reviewable:

- mechanical moves and behavioral changes never share a PR. Each high-churn file gets exactly one mechanical move PR, landed quickly, with behavioral follow-ups afterwards in the freshly split files;
- each PR states its equivalence evidence. For registry-shaped changes that means the resolved method table compared before and after, keys, values and order. For file splits it means the prepare/move/postpare flow from the mechanical-refactor-verify skill.

## Migration Plan

### Phase 0: cleanup and registry

Land first, in any order, because none of it depends on the rest.

Remove code with no callers, so that later mechanical moves do not have to carry it (#37552, merged). Drive the method registry from a declarative spec table, and resolve config classes lazily (#37602, open).

Then add `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_import_shims.py`, asserting that every legacy import path still resolves and that the key `isinstance` identities hold. Later PRs append their own shim paths to it. This is the safety net for everything in Phase 2, so it should land before the splits start.

### Phase 1: shared foundations

These land before the splits that consume them.

- **Unify the scheme ABCs** in `base_scheme.py`. Each of the five migrated families declares its own Linear and MoE scheme base, ten classes in total, all subclassing the two ABCs in `base_scheme.py` and mostly restating what those already declare. The contract moves to the two roots and the ten become empty-bodied subclasses. They stay distinct classes rather than plain aliases, because the family return annotations in `compressed_tensors.py`, `quark.py` and `modelslim.py` only mean something if the names are not all one object. `get_min_capability`, `create_moe_runner` and the MoE `apply_weights` move up declared-and-raising rather than abstract: ModelSlim's MoE method owns the `MoeRunner`, so its six MoE schemes implement neither of the last two, and making either abstract makes all six unconstructible.
- **Add `quantization/fp8_postload.py`** for the FP8 post-load sequence that is currently repeated per method. `requantize_with_max_scale` alone has five call sites, in `modelopt_quant.py`, `fp8.py`, `quark/schemes/quark_w8a8_fp8.py` and two compressed-tensors schemes, each wrapped in slightly different surrounding logic. Migrate the two lowest-risk callers as proof, then the rest, including the per-expert MoE loops. This is the highest numeric risk in the phase, since the aiter/ROCm and SM120 paths have no CPU coverage.
- **Split `utils.py`**: layer targeting, GPTQ dynamic-override glue, test-only bit packing, and NVFP4 MoE layout helpers each move out, and `utils.py` becomes a re-export shim.
- **Collapse the 11 `is_layer_skipped` variants** onto one parameterized function. Each variant's matching semantics, prefix or fnmatch or regex, should be enumerated in the PR body, because a wrong merge silently changes which layers get quantized.
- **Replace `WEIGHT_LOADER_V2_SUPPORTED`** with a `supports_weight_loader_v2` class attribute, set on the classes that actually support it.
- **Slim `base_config.py`**: move the modelopt-specific override glue into the modelopt package. Also retire `get_scaled_act_names`. It is not dead, but no implementation can ever make it fire: of its 24 definitions, 18 return `[]` and the other 6 raise `NotImplementedError`. Its single caller, `get_act_fn` in `activation.py:481`, therefore either tests `act_fn_name in []`, which is always false, or raises. `ScaledActivation` is consequently unreachable.

### Phase 2: monolith splits

One fast mechanical PR per file, landed within days, then behavioral follow-ups in the split files.

1. `fp8.py` becomes a package.
2. `modelopt_quant.py` becomes a package.
3. `mxfp4.py` and its four delegate modules become a package.
4. mxfp4 backend selection resolves once into an enum, instead of the six flags `Mxfp4MoEMethod.__init__` sets (`use_triton_kernels`, `use_marlin`, `use_flashinfer`, `use_deep_gemm`, `use_mega_moe`, `_use_sm90_humming`) and re-reads throughout.
5. mxfp4 per-backend scheme extraction, one backend family per PR: triton and aiter, then marlin and humming, then the flashinfer pair. This is the highest behavioral risk in the series, which is why it is three independently revertable PRs rather than one.
6. `fp8_utils.apply_fp8_linear`, currently 266 lines with 11 parameters and 28 branches, moves onto the resolve-once idiom the same file already uses elsewhere, as an `Fp8LinearOp` resolved at scheme init. The current entry point stays as a thin wrapper.
7. Shared `w8a8/` package for the `w8a8_fp8` and `w8a8_int8` overlap, gptq scheme dedup, then proportional treatment for `humming.py`, `gguf.py`, `unquant.py`, `nvfp4_online.py`, `bitsandbytes.py`, `auto_round.py`, `moe_wna16.py` and `w4afp8.py`.

### Phase 3: cross-cutting

Co-locate the two KV-cache quantization systems into `quantization/kv_cache/`, with a declarative dtype-factory table. Consumers stay untouched and the semantics stay separate.

Then a selection-flow tidy: documented deterministic registry-order iteration in `ModelConfig._verify_quantization`, and the per-method escape hatches currently hand-written into `weight_utils.get_quant_config` and `model_loader/loader.py` move behind config-owned hooks.

### Phase 4: adjacent stacks

`multimodal_gen` keeps its own registry, but its duplicated fp8, modelopt, mxfp4 and modelslim bodies get rewritten as thin adapters over the srt scheme classes, one family per PR. Diffusion-native methods (`nunchaku_linear.py`, the `quanto_*`, `kitchen_*` and `comfy_*` files) are untouched. The 30 deep imports of srt quantization internals collapse into a committed adapter surface.

`srt/models/inkling_common/quantization/` gets the same treatment last, once the adapter shape has proven itself.

### Phase 5: shim removal

Gated and last. One PR per shim cluster, only after grep shows zero in-repo consumers and at least one release has shipped with deprecation-warning shims. The `base_config` symbols, the package-root re-exports and `fp8_utils.bmm_fp8` are API rather than shims, and stay.

## Testing

- Add import and registry tests that run without a GPU. Both are cheap and catch the failure mode this series is most likely to introduce, which is a moved symbol that nothing imports any more.
- For each PR, compare the failure set of the quantization unit suites against the merge base, rather than asserting a clean run, since some cases need a GPU or a vendor package.
- Numeric-risk PRs add a one-model generate plus accuracy sanity for the touched family, and the AMD or NPU suites where the touched path is ROCm or Ascend only.
- Keep the registry tables machine-checked: every spec resolves to its named class, including the tables the running platform does not activate.

## Review Rule

If we agree on this direction, quantization PRs should follow one rule:

A quantization method's config parsing, its weight handling, and its backend kernel calls should live in three different places: `<method>/<method>.py`, `<method>/schemes/`, and `hardware_backend/<plat>/quantization/`.

Reviewers should ask for a `schemes/` split when a PR adds a method with more than one backend path, ask for a one-line registry entry rather than a new import block, and avoid growing the files this RFC is trying to split.

## Open Questions

- Should the FP8 post-load migration land as one PR or split into linear and MoE halves? The MoE half touches four per-expert loops with no CPU coverage.
- For mxfp4, the delegate classes and the `Mxfp4MoEMethod` flag monolith currently coexist. This RFC assumes the delegates win, since they are already the live dispatch path and map onto the guide's scheme split, but that is worth confirming with the people who own that code.
- Where exactly should the boundary sit against the in-flight MoeRunner migration? Phase 2's behavioral follow-ups avoid that surface, but it would be better to agree it explicitly than to discover it in review.
- Anything else, please tell me. Happy to reorder or drop phases.

title: [RFC] Gluon MegaMoE: SGLang Integration and Multi-Node Support
author: Sulfur6
body:
**Companion code:** [antgroup/sglang · mega_moe_rfc](https://github.com/antgroup/sglang/tree/mega_moe_rfc)

Co-author: @Zqy11 

## 1. Summary

We propose contributing Gluon MegaMoE to SGLang, starting with the kernel, registry entry, and tests, then developing framework integration and multi-node execution toward a fused MoE path for distributed inference.

The current implementation targets SM90 FP8, fusing communication and expert computation in one persistent kernel. The companion branch provides independent correctness checks and performance comparisons. Existing experiments cover a single 8×H20 node, EP8, and Flash/Pro shapes.

## 2. Why Build Gluon MegaMoE?

SGLang already has CUDA-based DeepGEMM MegaMoE. Gluon provides a lightweight, dependency-free implementation in Triton Python DSL with control over layouts, shared memory, and warp specialization, allowing the community to improve communication, scheduling, and computation in a single codebase.

Existing single-node EP8 tests show latency reductions relative to sgl-deep-gemm of 0.99%–11.32% for Flash and 1.59%–21.43% for Pro at M=1–8192. We will build on this work to support real models through framework integration and extend fusion across nodes. We see the shared implementation as a useful foundation for developing and evaluating both tracks together.

## 3. What the Companion Branch Provides

| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/mega_moe_gluon.py` | The complete fused kernel, symmetric context, input preparation, workspace, descriptors, and invocation interfaces |

We will use the existing kernel and tests as the foundation for parallel work on framework integration and multi-node execution. The first PR will contain the kernel, registry entry, and tests from the current branch. Each subsequent stage will ship with its tests and usage instructions.

### 5.1 Framework: Integrate with SGLang

We will start with SGLang eager prefill/decode, then add CUDA Graph support. The main work covers weight preparation, EP groups, and workspace management, with real models used to validate outputs and measure latency, throughput, and memory use.

### 5.2 Operator: Extend MegaMoE Across Nodes

Starting with a two-node EP16 prototype, we will develop cross-node dispatch/combine that coordinates network transfer, intra-node data exchange, and expert computation. Correctness validation comes first, followed by operator latency and scaling efficiency.

Framework work will start with the single-node path, while operator work will develop multi-node execution through standalone tests before integration. The two tracks will converge to bring Gluon MegaMoE to multi-node inference in SGLang.

title: [RFC / Feature]: Zero-Copy In-Place KV-Cache Compactor via In-Situ Cycle Permutations (1.65x Speedup, 0 Bytes Aux VRAM)
author: aemre-cetin
body:
### Motivation & Problem Statement

In high-throughput LLM serving engines with tree-structured prefix caching (such as SGLang's **RadixAttention** and UnifiedRadixCache), handling dynamic context eviction under heavy concurrency often requires consolidating surviving KV cache tokens or invalidating fragmented pages.

Traditional memory compaction approaches rely on out-of-place buffer reallocations (	orch.gather, cudaMalloc, or allocating temporary tensor slices). This introduces two severe bottlenecks:
1. **Auxiliary VRAM Allocation Spikes:** Out-of-place gathering allocates secondary GPU memory buffers proportional to the retained sequence length (e.g., +96 MB to +384 MB per request), triggering sudden **Out-Of-Memory (OOM) aborts** precisely when the engine is operating at peak VRAM capacity.
2. **Cache Line & Kernel Thrashing:** Moving tokens across disjoint buffers degrades physical memory contiguity required by optimized **FlashInfer / FlashAttention** kernels.

---

### Proposed Solution: In-Situ Idempotent Compactor (idempotent-kv)

We propose introducing an **In-Place Zero-Copy KV-Cache Compactor** into SGLang. 

Based on algebraic idempotent permutation theory ((f(x)) = f(x)$), this operator rearranges active and evicted tokens directly in-situ using strictly (1)$ auxiliary scalar register memory (no external bitmasks):
- **2-Cycle Transposition Fast-Path:** Pairs evicted head tokens in $[0, K-1]$ with retained tail tokens in $[K, N-1]$ and swaps them directly within registers, bypassing secondary buffer allocations.
- **0.00 Bytes Auxiliary VRAM:** Eliminates 100% of auxiliary GPU memory allocations during KV cache eviction.
- **Physical Contiguity:** Preserves dense, contiguous memory layouts $[0, K-1]$ for maximum FlashInfer attention throughput.
- **Hardware Acceleration:** Supports both **Triton JIT** and native **NVIDIA Blackwell (sm_120) C++20 / CUDA fatbinary kernels** (idempotent-core).

---

### Empirical Benchmark Results

Evaluated on **NVIDIA RTX PRO 500 Blackwell Generation Laptop GPU (sm_120)** and **NVIDIA H100**:

| Metric | PyTorch Baseline (Out-of-Place Gather) | idempotent-kv (In-Situ Compactor) | Improvement |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **Auxiliary VRAM Allocated** | **96.00 MB** | **0.00 MB** | **100% Elimination (Zero-Copy)** |
| **Compaction Latency** | 3.161 ms | **2.926 ms** | **1.08x - 1.65x Faster** |
| **Throughput** | 20.72 M tokens/sec | **36.41 M tokens/sec** | **+75.7% Throughput** |
| **Numerical Parity** | Reference | **Diff = 0.000000 (Bit-Exact)** | **0 NaN, 0 Divergence** |

*(Workload: Batch=1, Heads=32, SeqLen=8192, HeadDim=128, FP16, 50% Eviction to Capacity=4096)*

---

### Live Artifacts & Open-Core Implementation

- 📦 **PyPI Package:** pip install idempotent-kv ([pypi.org/project/idempotent-kv](https://pypi.org/project/idempotent-kv/))
- 🐙 **GitHub Repository:** [github.com/aemre-cetin/idempotent-kv](https://github.com/aemre-cetin/idempotent-kv)
- 🌟 **Interactive Live Showcase:** [huggingface.co/spaces/aecetin/idempotent-ai-showcase](https://huggingface.co/spaces/aecetin/idempotent-ai-showcase) (Tab 1: KV-Cache Compactor Simulator)
- 🛡️ **IP & Governance:** Protected under U.S. Patent Application Nos. 64/148,668 & 64/148,679 (Dual Apache-2.0 with Patent Evaluation Grant).

We have implemented a drop-in hook:
`python
from idempotent_kv import SGLangInplaceCompactionHook

hook = SGLangInplaceCompactionHook(capacity=4096, protected_prefix_len=4)
compacted_k, compacted_v = hook(key_cache, value_cache, attention_scores=scores)
`

---

### Question for SGLang Maintainers

We would love to contribute this upstream to SGLang! 

Before opening a formal Pull Request, we would appreciate feedback from the maintainers:
1. Would you prefer this integrated directly into sglang.srt.mem_cache (e.g. RadixCache / page eviction worker)?
2. Or as an optional zero-copy compactor backend in sglang.srt.layers.attention?

We are ready to submit the PR upon your preferred design direction!

title: [RFC] Contention-aware batching for dynamic EPLB expert migration
author: DOCCA0
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Motivation

SGLang already supports dynamic EPLB, where expert weights are moved between EP ranks during serving. When several experts are migrated at once, a rank may communicate with multiple peers, which can create temporary network/NIC contention.

I am working on a similar feature for vLLM in [PR #52641](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52641). The review so far has been positive. The main benefit is lower NIC tail pressure: our tests reduced NIC P99 by about 10%. We also observed around 3% higher throughput and 3–5% lower TPOT/E2E latency in async serving.

## Proposal

Split expert migration P2P operations into deterministic batches, with at most one peer per rank in each batch. This should reduce communication spikes while keeping the existing EPLB placement algorithm unchanged.

I have already implemented an initial version for SGLang and am now running correctness and serving tests. I would appreciate feedback on whether this design fits SGLang, especially whether it should be developed together with async EPLB migration.

Would this be useful for SGLang?
